title: STM Warrant - October 20, 2026
text: TOWN OF HARVARD MASSACHUSETTS Special Town Meeting Warrant October 20, 2026 @6:00pm The Bromfield School Cronin Auditorium 14 Massachusetts Ave TABLE OF CONTENTS Ar cle # Ar cle Name Page # 1 Pay Bills of Prior Fiscal Years 2 2 School ESSER Grant Deﬁcit 2 3 Capital Planning and Investment Commi ee Recommended Expenditure 3 4 3 5 Amend General Bylaw – Chapter 78 Personnel Bylaw Sec ons 78-6C Problem Resolu on and 78-7 Employee Beneﬁts Replace Current § 125-53 with new Clean Energy Facili es Bylaw 6 Amend Chapter 125 (Protec ve Bylaw) to Conform with M.G.L. Ch. 40A 7 7 Reorganiza on of Chapter 125 Pertaining to Use Regula ons 8 8 Reorganiza on of Chapter 125 Pertaining to Dimensional Regula ons 9 9 Revise §125-60 MBTA Communi es Mul -family Overlay District 9 A achments - Zoning Ar cles #5-9 Proposed Changes 12 October 20, 2026 Special Town Meeting Warrant 1 6 WARRANT FOR THE 2026 TOWN OF HARVARD SPECIAL TOWN MEETING COMMONWEALTH OF MASSACHUSETTS Worcester, ss. To the Constable of the Town of Harvard Greetings: In the name of the Commonwealth, you are hereby required to notify and warn the inhabitants of the said Town, who are qualified to vote in Town Affairs, to meet at the Bromfield School Auditorium, located at 14 Massachusetts Avenue, on Tuesday the 20th day of October, 2026 at 6:00 PM by the clock to act on the following articles. ARTICLE 1: PAY BILLS OF PRIOR FISCAL YEARS To see if the Town will vote to raise and appropriate, borrow, or transfer from available funds a sum of money to pay bills from Fiscal Year 2026, or pass any vote or votes in relation thereto. (Inserted by Finance Director) Summary: Town Meeting approval is required to pay bills from a prior fiscal year. A list of unpaid bills will be provided at Town Meeting. Select Board Recommendations: The Board unanimously recommends this Article. Finance Committee Recommendations: The Committee unanimously recommends this Article. ARTICLE 2: SCHOOL ESSER GRANT DEFICIT To see if the Town will vote to raise and appropriate, borrow, or transfer from available funds the sum of $14,934 in order to cover the deficit resulting from the overspending of the Fiscal Year 2022 ESSER III grant funds in Fiscal Year 2026. (Inserted by School Committee) Summary: During the current closeout and reconciliation of the ESSER III grant, an issue was identified related to professional staff expenditures and it was found that payment of the MTRS contributions was not completed prior to the end of the grant period in FY2022. In order to satisfy that requirement, the district has made the required payment to cover the FY2022 payment but has now overexpanded the current FY grant. This transfer will cover the over expenditure and allow the district to close out the FY2022 fiscal year grant. October 20, 2026 Special Town Meeting Warrant 2 Select Board Recommendations: The Board unanimously recommends this Article. Finance Committee Recommendations: The Committee unanimously recommends this Article. ARTICLE 3: CAPITAL PLANNING AND INVESTMENT COMMITTEE RECOMMENDED EXPENDITURE To see if the Town will vote to raise and appropriate, borrow, or transfer from available funds, the following sums of money to be expended by the following boards and officials for the capital projects and acquisitions described and numbered below, each of which shall be a separate appropriation, and to provide for said appropriations from the Capital Stabilization Fund, and that any funds remaining will be returned to their funding source, or pass any vote or votes in relation thereto. (Inserted by the Capital Planning and Investment Committee) 1 Board or Oﬃcial Descrip on of Acquisi on or Authorized to Expend Funds Project Amount Funding Source Police Department - Police Cruiser Police Chief with Select Board approval $80,122 Capital Stabilization Fund DPW Director with Select Board approval $55,000 Capital Stabilization Fund 2 DPW – Water Meters Summary: This capital request is for the scheduled replacement of the Police Department’s oldest frontline patrol unit. The vehicle being requested is a Police Interceptor Utility Hybrid vehicle. The request is also for replacement of water meters. This will allow the DPW to complete the water meter replacement project that was started a year ago. Once this is complete, all meters will have been upgraded to the latest technology which will help with meter reads and accuracy with billing. Select Board Recommendations: The Board unanimously recommends this Article . Finance Committee Recommendations: The Committee did not take a position on this article. ARTICLE 4: AMEND GENERAL BYLAW – CHAPTER 78 PERSONNEL BYLAW SECTIONS 78-6C PROBLEM RESOLUTION AND 78-7 EMPLOYEE BENEFITS To see if the Town will vote to amend Chapter 78 of the Code of the Town of Harvard, Personnel Bylaw by making the following revision to Section 78-6C and deleting Section 78-7 in its entirety; or take any other action relative thereto. October 20, 2026 Special Town Meeting Warrant 3 (Inserted by Personnel Board) § 78-6 Problem resolution. C. If this conference fails to clear up any question to the satisfaction of the employee, he the employee may refer the matter in writing to the appropriate appointing authority. The appointing authority shall then discuss the matter with the parties and attempt to reach a satisfactory understanding and solution of the problem. § 78-7Employee benefits. The beneﬁts for employees covered by this bylaw shall include but not be limited to the following: A. Paid me oﬀ (PTO). Regular employees are en tled to paid me oﬀ each year based on the amount of con nuous service origina ng with the date of hire using the following schedule: [Amended 3-27-1999 ATM by Art. 32; 10-10-2007 STM by Art. 10] PTO Years of Service (days) 1 25 2 26 3 27 4 28 5 29 6 30 7 31 8 32 9 33 10 34 11 or more 35 B. (Reserved)[1] [1] Editor's Note: Former Subsec on B, Sick days, was repealed 10-10-2007 STM by Art. 10. See now Subsec on A. C. Other excused absences. Absences with pay may be excused by supervisors without charge to vaca on for court leave, military leave, bereavement leave (no more than three days), vo ng (when not prac cable to vote otherwise), and emergencies. D. Leave without pay. A temporary non-pay status and absence from work granted by the Town at the employee's request. October 20, 2026 Special Town Meeting Warrant 4 E. Re rement/health insurance. For the purpose of re rement health insurance, an employee must have been a "regular" municipal/county/state employee with 10 years of con nuous service in which he/she was eligible for beneﬁt coverage and, at a minimum, age 55. F. Over me. Over me shall not be paid to employees of the Town except as provided in this subsec on: (1) When over me work is requested by the head of the department concerned, nonexempt employees shall receive pay on the following basis: (a) Nonexempt employees will be paid at 1 1/2 mes their base pay for hours worked in excess of 40 hours worked per week. For payroll calcula ons, holiday and vaca on shall be considered as hours worked. (b) Employees recalled to work from oﬀ-duty hours will receive a minimum of three hours' pay. Police will receive a minimum of three hours' pay at their regular base pay for court me only. (2) Exempt salaried employees do not receive over me. These employees by federal law are not required to receive over me compensa on. G. Holidays. The following shall be considered holidays: New Year's Day Independence Day Mar n Luther King Day Labor Day Presidents Day Columbus Day[2] Patriots Day Veterans Day Memorial Day Thanksgiving Day Christmas Day [2] Editor's Note: At the 5-14-2022 ATM, by Art. 30, the Town voted to change "Columbus Day" to "Indigenous People's Day" throughout all documents currently in use by the Town. H. Workers' compensa on. An employee who by reason of an industrial accident receives statutory compensa on may receive, in addi on, the amount necessary to make up his regular weekly compensa on only to the extent of the person's accumulated sick and vaca on me applied on October 20, 2026 Special Town Meeting Warrant 5 a pro rata basis. I. A deferred compensa on program shall be established. All employees with ﬁve or more years of con nuous service with the Town are eligible. Employees may elect to contribute any amount up to 5% of their base salary, as determined by the compensa on plan. Such contribu ons will be forwarded directly to the vendor for credit to the employee's account. The Town will match the employee's contribu ons according to the following schedule: [Added 3-31-1990 ATM by Art. 16] (1) Employees with ﬁve but less than 10 years of service on July 1 will have their contribu ons matched at the rate of 15%. (2) Employees with 10 but less than 20 years of service on July 1 will have their contribu ons matched at the rate of 25%. (3) Employees with 20 or more years of service on July 1 will have their contribu ons matched at the rate of 50%. Summary: These changes formalize provisions that were previously governed by the Personnel Bylaw but have since been incorporated into the Town’s Personnel Policies and Procedures. The changes codify practices that are already in place. Select Board Recommendations: The Board unanimously recommends this Article. Finance Committee Recommendations: The Committee did not take a position on this article. ARTICLE 5: REPLACE CURRENT §125-53 WITH NEW CLEAN ENERGY FACILITIES BYLAW To see if the Town will vote to amend Chapter 125 (Protective Bylaw) of the Town of Harvard as follows: 1. Replace §125-53 (Large-Scale Ground-Mounted Solar Photovoltaic Facilities Overlay District, added 11-9-2010 STM by Art. 2, amended 8-29-2012 STM by Art. 2) in its entirety; and 2. Insert a new §125-53 titled "Clean Energy Facilities," as set forth in the document on file with the Town Clerk, incorporating standards for Solar Photovoltaic Installations, Battery Energy Storage Systems, and Consolidated Local Permitting consistent with 225 CMR 29.00 and Chapter 239 of the Acts of 2024; or take any other action relative thereto. (Inserted by Planning Board) October 20, 2026 Special Town Meeting Warrant 6 Summary: The current solar overlay district needs replacing because of a new state permitting law (Chapter 239 of the Acts of 2024) and recent court decisions. Case law has made the current overlay-district structure legally vulnerable. Under the Dover Amendment (M.G.L. c. 40A, § 3), courts have repeatedly struck down zoning that confines solar too narrowly. The proposed bylaw establishes local siting standards and a consolidated permitting process for solar energy systems, and for the first time, includes standards for battery energy storage systems (BESS). Select Board Recommendations: The Board unanimously recommends this Article. Finance Committee Recommendations: The Committee did not take a position on this article. ARTICLE 6: AMEND CHAPTER 125 (PROTECTIVE BYLAW) TO CONFORM WITH M.G.L. CH. 40A To see if the Town will vote to amend Chapter 125 (Protective Bylaw) of the Town of Harvard as follows:  Amend §§125-3 (Non-conforming Structures and Uses), 125-4 (Exis ng Lots), 125-45 (Board of Appeals), 125-46 (Special Permits), and 125-49 (Enforcement) to conform to recent amendments to the Zoning Act, M.G.L. Chapter 40A, enacted by the FY2027 state budget (House Bill 5555, eﬀec ve July 1, 2026), including revised variance standards, dura ons, and extension periods; protec ons for pre-exis ng nonconforming uses and structures; abandonment determina on melines; zoning freeze periods; and lot merger protec ons. or take any other action relative thereto. (Inserted by Planning Board) Summary: This article amends Chapter 125 (Protective Bylaw)§§ 125-3, 125-4, 125-45, 125-46, and 125-49 to conform Harvard's zoning bylaw to recent amendments to the Zoning Act, M.G.L. Chapter 40A, enacted by the FY2027 state budget (House Bill 5555, effective July 1, 2026). The revisions update the Town's variance standard to the new "practical difficulty" test, extend the special permit and variance validity periods, and expand protections for pre-existing nonconforming structures, uses, and lots, including a longer abandonment determination period and new lot merger protections. The article also corrects several provisions that had fallen out of conformance with earlier, unrelated amendments to Chapter 40A, including special permit duration limits and the maximum penalty for zoning violations. No new use, density, or dimensional standards are being introduced in this revision. This is strictly a housekeeping amendment to bring the bylaw's text into agreement with existing state law. Select Board Recommendations: The Board unanimously recommends this Article. Finance Committee Recommendations: The Committee did not take a position on this article. October 20, 2026 Special Town Meeting Warrant 7 ARTICLE 7: REORGANIZATION OF CHAPTER 125 PERTAINING TO USE REGULATIONS To see if the Town will vote to amend Chapter 125 (Protective Bylaw) of the Town of Harvard as follows: 1. Replace §125-6 (Intent), §125-7 (Agricultural uses), §125-8 (Single residence use), §125-9 (Mul ple residence use), §125-10 (Conversion for mul ple residence), §125-11 (Conversion of seasonal residence), §125-12 (Small-scale commercial uses), §125-13 (Medium-scale commercial uses), §125-14 (Large-scale commercial uses), §125-15 (Earthmoving), §125-16 (Ins tu onal uses), §125-17 (Oﬀ-site uses), §125-19 (Applicability), §125-20 (General), §125-21 (Permi ed uses in AR Districts), §125-22 (Permi ed Uses in B District), §125-23 (Permi ed uses in C Districts), and §125-24 (Permi ed uses in MR Districts) in their en rety; 2. Insert a new §125-19, tled "Use Regula ons," and a new §125-20, tled "Use Standards," establishing general use provisions, detailed use standards, and a Table of Uses; 3. Reserve §§125-6 through 125-17 and §§125-21 through 125-24; and 4. Re tle Ar cle III from "Use Groupings" to [reserved], and Ar cle IV from "Permi ed Uses by District" to "Use Regula ons;" and 5. Add the following new deﬁni ons to §125-2, Deﬁni ons: Auto Body Shop; Banks, Business Services, and Professional Oﬃce; Dry Cleaning and Laundry Pick-up Sta on; General Retail Sales and Services; Marijuana Cul vator; Media Produc on (with Support Facili es and Full-Service Facili es as subsec ons thereof); Motor Vehicle Repair Services; and Senior Residen al Development. 6. Amend §125-70C, Use, to replace the reference to “§125-23” with “§125-19 and Table 1.” or take any other action relative thereto. (Inserted by Planning Board) Summary: This article replaces the current scattered use provisions (§§125-19 through 125-24) with a single new §125-19, consolidating all permitted uses and required permits into one Table of Uses. It's part of the Planning Board's ongoing effort to simplify the bylaw so residents can see, district by district, exactly what's allowed and what permit each use requires. There are no new initiatives being introduced within this article. The change is a reorganization and clarification of existing rules, not a change in what's currently allowed. Select Board Recommendations: The Board unanimously recommends this Article. Finance Committee Recommendations: The Committee did not take a position on this article. October 20, 2026 Special Town Meeting Warrant 8 ARTICLE 8: REORGANIZATION OF CHAPTER 125 PERTAINING TO DIMENSIONAL REGULATIONS To see if the Town will vote to amend Chapter 125 (Protective Bylaw) of the Town of Harvard as follows: 1. Replace §§125-29 and 125-30 in its entirety; and 2. Insert a new table under §125-29; or take any other action relative thereto. (Inserted by Planning Board) Summary: This article replaces the Town's current lot size and setback rules (§§125-29 and 12530) with a reorganized §125-29 that consolidates all dimensional standards into a single table by zoning district. It simplifies how lot types are presented, making it easier for residents to identify which standards apply to their property. The change is a reorganization and clarification of existing rules, not a change in what's currently allowed. Select Board Recommendations: The Board unanimously recommends this Article. Finance Committee Recommendations: The Committee did not take a position on this article. ARTICLE 9: REVISE §125-60 MBTA COMMUNITIES MULTI-FAMILY OVERLAY DISTRICT To see if the Town will vote to amend Chapter 125 (Protective Bylaw) of the Town of Harvard as follows: 1. Amend §125-60, MBTA Communi es Mul -Family Overlay District, to clarify the applicability of the inclusionary zoning requirement within the overlay district and to make other clarifying and correc ve revisions to the provisions of that sec on. or take any other action relative thereto. (Inserted by Planning Board) Summary: This amendment clarifies how the inclusionary affordable housing requirement applies within the overlay district and makes other corrective and clarifying revisions. These are refinements to an already-adopted district, not a change to its core standards. Select Board Recommendations: The Board unanimously recommends this Article. Finance Committee Recommendations: The Committee did not take a position on this article. *** October 20, 2026 Special Town Meeting Warrant 9 Proposed Changes for Zoning Articles #5-9 October 20, 2026 Special Town Meeting Warrant 11 Draft Zoning Article – FINAL for Warrant Article 5 - §125-53 (Clean Energy Facilities Bylaw) Last Edit date: September 28, 2026 ARTICLE 5: Clean Energy Facilities Bylaw Summary: The current solar overlay district needs replacing because of a new state permitting law (Chapter 239 of the Acts of 2024) and recent court decisions. The proposed bylaw establishes local siting standards and a consolidated permitting process for solar energy systems, and for the ﬁrst time, includes standards for battery energy storage systems (BESS). To see if the Town will vote to amend Chapter 125 (Protective Bylaw) of the Town of Harvard as follows: 1. A. Purpose. This section establishes standards for Solar Photovoltaic Installations, Battery Energy Storage Systems (BESS), and other Small Clean Energy Infrastructure Facilities (SCEIFs) throughout the Town of Harvard, consistent with M.G.L. c. 40A, § 3, 225 CMR 29.00, and Chapter 239 of the Acts of 2024. Standards address public safety, scenic and natural resource protection, and ﬁnancial assurance for decommissioning. B. Applicability. This § 125-53 applies to Solar Photovoltaic Installations and BESS Installations proposed for construction after the e ective date of this section, and to SCEIFs electing the Consolidated Local Permit pathway under Subsection F(1). Material modiﬁcations to existing facilities are governed by Subsection E(4)(b). C. Deﬁnitions. For purposes of this § 125-53, the following deﬁnitions apply. Accessory Use: A solar or BESS installation is considered an Accessory Use when it is subordinate and customarily incidental to the permitted primary use of the premises. Tuesday, October 6, 2026 6:30 PM AGENDA PRESIDENT’S REPORT PUBLIC HEARING PUBLIC COMMENT REGULAR AND PENDING EXECUTIVE SESSION MINUTES 1. June 11, 2024, September 4, 2024, and April 15, 2025 Executive Session Minutes – Reviewed and ready for partial release as of September 17, 2025 2. December 9, 2024 Finance Committee Executive Session Minutes – Reviewed and withheld in entirety as of September 17, 2025 3. From City Clerk Brenna Murphy Leary and Admin. Assistant Jeffery Anderson-Burgos- meeting minutes from September 15, 2026 LAID ON THE TABLE 4. Vacon- Greaney- ORDER: that city council go to the first ballot to elect a treasurer at the April 21, 2026 city council meeting in accordance with our current charter. Our city council appointed Collector has indicated interest in the Treasurer/Collector position. A majority of the city council has had the opportunity to interview our Collector. This appointment would legally establish the Treasurer position & for practical purposes combines the positions, while waiting for further charter changes that will be sent to the state legislature in a home rule petition. Transition changes can happen in coordination with other ordinance changes. COMMUNICATIONS 5. From Mayor Joshua Garcia-communication regarding the City Forestry Crew 6. From Mayor Joshua Garcia- letter appointing Mr. Stephen Fay of 218 Pleasant St. to serve as an alternate of the new Historical Commission. Mr. Fay’s term will expire on July 1, 2029. 7. From Mayor Joshua Garica-letter appointing Ms. Rebecca Lisi of 25 Reservation Rd. to serve on the Holyoke Redevelopment Authority. Ms. Lisi will replace Mr. Thomas Creed and will serve the remainder of his term, expiring November 1, 2026. 8. From Police Chief Brian Keenan-Policy and Procedure Automatic License Plate Recognition 9. From City of Holyoke Health Benefit Meeting Minutes July 15, 2026 10. From the Holyoke Redevelopment Authority-meeting minutes from June 17, July 15 and August 19, 2026. 11. From City Comptroller Sharon Bittner-Willis, FY2027 General Fund Expense YTD Report-Totals 12. From City Comptroller Sharon Bittner-Willis, FY2027 Sewer Enterprise Expense YTD Report-Totals 13. Petition from various residents regarding voting against cancelling Columbus Day PETITIONS 14. Petition from Roxanne Roman of 76 Elmwood Ave for a zone change from RA to R-2 to develop two duplexes on the vacant parcel 15. Petition from Daphine Nyachowe or 601 Northampton St for a Livery License 16. Petition from Carlos Colon for a Street Vendor License at 920 Main St. for a food truck REPORTS OF COMMITTEES 17. The Committee on Ordinance to whom was referred a Zone change application from BG (business general) to DR (downtown residential) of Irfan Raheel at 172 Sargeant Street (060-06-001) to allow for second floor residential use. Recommended that the zone change be granted. 18. The Committee on Ordinance to whom was referred an order that the Honorable City Council review the ordinance that establishes the operating time frames for cannabis dispensaries. Recommended that the order be adopted. 19. The Committee on Ordinance to whom was referred an order that ordinance sections 2-38 and 2-39 be revised to replace “Columbus Day” with “Indigenous Peoples’ Day.” Recommended that the order be adopted. 20. The Committee on Ordinance to whom was referred an order that the DPW install a Handicap Sign for Luis Davila of 240 Walnut St. #PL8720803 Recommended that the order be adopted. 21. The Committee on Ordinance to whom was referred an order that the handicap parking sign located at 107 Brown Ave be removed as the tenant who originally requested and utilized it has moved and the space is no longer needed. Recommended that the order be adopted. 22. The Committee on Ordinance to whom was referred an order that the City Council review Holyoke’s municipal rules, ordinances, and any related materials that may be discovered during the process of review, relatiing to notices to citizens of proposed changes in the Zoning Ordinance and publication of such notices, and make such amendments to our ordinances and rules that may be found desirable in light of that review. While required notices are set forth in state law, a review of our local ordinances, etc., may reveal inefficiencies that are not required by said state law. This order is intended to be broadly construed to cover any public notice requirements, with respect to any other matters, that may be found to be affected by such municipal rules or ordinances. Recommended that the order has been complied with. 23. The Committee on Ordinance to whom was referred an order that any person who is a realtor or owns a real estate business who is appointed by the Mayor to the Planning Board and confirmed by the City Council SHALL recuse themselves from any zoning vote that would enrich them or their business unless they receive written approval from the State Conflict of Interest department. Recommended that the order has been complied with. 24. The Committee on Ordinance to whom was referred an order that the Planning Board be invited to appear in person if possible to the September meeting of the Ordinance Committee. Recommended that the order has been complied with. 25. The Committee on Ordinance to whom was referred an order that Council make the necessary zoning ordinance changes in order for us to clarify parking on residential properties and create an enforcement structure. Recommended that the order be given a leave to withdraw. 26. The Committee on Ordinance to whom was referred a Petition of Paola M. Rosado Freytiz of 71 Brown Ave Apt 1 for street vendor license for food truck at 1810 Northampton Street. Awaiting disposition 27. The Committee on Ordinance to whom was referred an order that the Ordinance Committee increase the fines for any and all ordinances dealing with blocking driveways, crosswalks and parking too close to intersections, and any other citable offenses listed on the attached sample parking ticket. Fines shall be increased to $75 and up to $150. Any violation of the parking ban shall be a fine of $150. In addition, if warranted, a payment plan may be implemented for low income and elderly residents. Awaiting disposition 28. The Committee on Ordinance to whom was referred an order that the fines be increased for illegal dumping, especially construction equipment and garbage on a sidewalk or street that has not been recycled. The word “rubbish” shall mean solid waste consisting of both combustible and non combustible wastes such as paper, wrappings, newsprint, cardboard, tin cans, yard clippings, leaves, glass, plastics (as in nip bottles) and bedding. Awaiting disposition 29. The Committee on Ordinance to whom was referred an order that the Sound Permitting Ordinance be amended to designate the License Board as the granting authority for sound permits, rather than the Chief of Police. This change is intended to align the permitting process with the License Board’s established role in reviewing, issuing, and regulating licenses, while ensuring a transparent, consistent, and civilian-led decision-making process. Transferring this authority would provide clearer standards, improved accountability, and greater procedural fairness for applicants, while allowing the Police Department to focus on enforcement and public safety responsibilities rather than administrative permitting functions. Awaiting disposition 30. The Committee on Ordinance to whom was referred an order that the City Council review Section 38-71 of the Holyoke Code of Ordinances and amend it as necessary to remove outdated exemptions therein. Awaiting disposition 31. The Committee on Ordinance to whom was referred an order The city council amend chapter 86 of the city’s ordinances (and elsewhere if so deemed) to allow two-wheeled vehicles (i.e. motorcycles) to park multiple like-sized vehicles in any single public parking space as the City Engineer may determine (potentially up to three) whether metered or not metered. This shall be applicable to parking spaces in city-owned parking garages including Mayor Taupier and Mayor Proulx. The city shall allow private parking lots the option to institute a similar parking schedule for motorcycles and like-sized vehicles. Alternatively, the city allow said right to be permitted by special permit issued by the Chief of Police if other traffic standards do not allow this ordinance change. City Council consider adoption of chapter 40, section 22 of MGL. Awaiting disposition 32. The Committee on Ordinance to whom was referred an order That an ordinance be created that will require an annual registration, liability insurance and an official Massachusetts license plate for high speed motorized bicycles. Awaiting disposition 33. The Committee on Ordinance to whom was referred an order That regulations be created through the Holyoke Police Department and/or an ordinance be created in accordance with MGL c90, s 1E as it relates to as “pocket bikes”, “mini bikes”, “mini motorcycles”, “motorized skateboards” and any other two-wheeled tandem or three-wheeled devices, that has handlebars, designed to be stood or sat upon by the operator, powered by an electric or gas powered motor that is capable or propelling the device with or without human propulsion, and is not defined as a motor vehicle or motorcycle under the law of the Commonwealth of Massachusetts, shall be considered as a “motorized scooter”. Awaiting disposition 34. The Committee on Ordinance to whom was referred an order that the City Council amend City Ordinance 6-2 Drinking Alcoholic Beverage on Public Street, Section (a) changed to include the following wording. “The drinking of alcoholic beverages by any persons while, upon any way or in any place to which the public has a right of access, or upon any way or in any place to which members of the public have access as invitees or licensees” Awaiting disposition 35. The Committee on Ordinance to whom was referred an order that the City change the use of the lot at the corner of Adam and South Summer from being a 24hr parking to a Residential Parking from 5pm to 7am. Morgan School Staff Parking from 7am- 5pm. Awaiting disposition 36. The Committee on Ordinance to whom was referred an order that 2 lanes from Linden Street onto Beech Street be designated as a left turn lane and a right turn lane and painted with the appropriate turn arrows. Awaiting disposition 37. The Committee on Ordinance to whom was referred an order that a crosswalk be added across Northampton Street at River Terrace. Awaiting disposition 38. The Committee on Ordinance to whom was referred an order that a crosswalk be added across Hampton Knolls where it intersects with Northampton Street. Awaiting disposition 39. The Committee on Ordinance to whom was referred an order that Sec. 54-18. on removal of shopping carts be revised to add that establishments who employ shopping carts must ensure that a locking wheel system is used and that businesses have a responsibility to maintain them/handle removal of carts. Review and revise the existing enforcement structure for carts found off property. Awaiting disposition 40. The Committee on Ordinance to whom was referred an order that the Clerk and the Law Department draft a list of ordinances that they have a record of being changed in the past that were never presented to Municode and thus not in the current “Adopted Ordinances Not Yet Codified” queue. Awaiting disposition 41. The Committee on Ordinance to whom was referred an order that our winter parking ordinance be revised as necessary for clarity, functionality, and flexibility based on constituent and DPW needs. Awaiting disposition 42. The Committee on Ordinance to whom was referred an order that sections 2-35 (b) (i), (ii), and (iv) of the code of ordinances be deleted to allow for hiring new employees above the mid range. Awaiting disposition 43. The Committee on Ordinance to whom was referred an order that the City Council President establish by ordinance a temporary ad-hoc committee to expire/sunset by June 30, 2027 to study and provide an analysis on the potential impacts of commercial data center development in Holyoke, including electrical demand, water consumption, environmental impacts, tax revenue, economic development opportunities, zoning considerations, public safety concerns, and best practices adopted by other municipalities, and to make recommendations to the City Council regarding potential zoning and permitting requirements. This Ad-Hoc Committee shall include one member from: Holyoke Gas and Electric Holyoke Water Works or Member of Water Commission Massachusetts Green High-Performing Computing Center Planning Board Conservation Commission Office of Planning and Development Community Member or Resident appointed by the City Council President City Council Awaiting disposition 44. The Committee on Ordinance to whom was referred an order that in accordance with Section 86-95 of the Holyoke Code of Ordinances, 90 degree diagonal parking be established on the southerly side of Westfield Road at the 224 Westfield Rd property beginning at a point approximately 510 feet easterly of Bray Park Drive to a point 85 feet farther east. Awaiting disposition 45. The Committee on Public Safety to whom was referred an order Invite Veterans Services Department Director Laddy Rua to an upcoming Public Safety meeting for a conversation highlighting the services they provide and render in Holyoke to support veterans, especially those dealing with Post-Traumatic Stress Disorder (PTSD). Recommended that the order has been complied with. 46. The Committee on Public Safety to whom was referred an order Invite the Holyoke Safe Neighborhood Initiative to an upcoming Public Safety meeting for a conversation highlighting the work that they are doing in Holyoke to create safe, healthy & economically viable neighborhoods through information sharing, identifying at-risk youth, referrals and community efforts. Recommended that the order has been complied with. 47. The Committee on Public Safety to whom was referred an order that city council takes steps to support neighborhoods who wish to establish a neighborhood watch to help prevent crime. Recommended that the order has been complied with. 48. The Committee on Public Safety to whom was referred an order that the City Council review the history, authorization, and all aspects of the use of Flock cameras in Holyoke, and of any other automated license plate technology (ALPR) that may be deployed or under consideration for deployment, in order to determine whether legislation is necessary to address any civil rights and privacy issues that may be implicated by the presence of this technology and to enact such legislation should it prove to be needed. The information needed for this review shall include but not be limited to the city’s contract with Flock, including details of any amendments thereto; information showing who authorized the installation and when, for what reasons; how much the contract costs the city and where it is in the budget; where the data from these ALPRs is or may be shared or queried; for how long it is preserved; how it is safeguarded from abuse and access for improper purposes or by unauthorized persons; and whether Holyoke’s and Flock’s terms and practices are in compliance with Massachusetts law regarding the sharing of data, particularly with federal agencies. The Holyoke Police Department and the Law Department are requested to provide all relevant data to the City Council to assist in this review. Recommended that the order has been complied with. 49. The Committee on Public Safety to whom was referred an order The City of Holyoke prohibit the use of GLOVE (Generated Low Output Voltage Emitter) gloves. Classified as a CD3 (conductive distraction and de-escalation device), these devices work differently from other incapacitation devices (stun guns, tasers) by shocking the skin to cause neuro-peripheral disruption rather than using probe projectiles or higher voltage neuro-muscular disruption. In other words, it inflicts localized pain on subjects in order to enforce compliance rather than muscular disruption provided by other devices. Recommended that the order has been complied with. 50. The Committee on Charter and Rules to whom was referred an order : That a new City Council rule be enacted as follows: During a City Council meeting if a councilor wants to take up an agenda item out of order that whenever possible let the President know PRIOR to the item being taken out of order. Recommended that the order be given a leave to withdraw. MOTIONS, ORDERS AND RESOLUTIONS 51. Vacon- ORDER: That Columbus Day & Indigenous People Day be named together in our ordinance. 52. Vacon- ORDER: When a legal notice is sent to citizens for a zone change, a summary explaining the effect of & rationale for the change, (similar to a ballot question summary) is provided with the notice. 53. Vacon- ORDER: that our auditor submit the audit plan as previously voted by the city council and appear at Finance Committee to present the audit plan. Send to Finance Committee & Auditor. 54. Vacon- ORDER: request the Board of Health to provide a report on the status of removal of kratom products from all stores in accordance with the statewide ban in effect as of 8/26226. 55. Vacon- ORDER: The Board of Registrars/City Clerk audit the November 2025 votes (to determine the cause of a 6 vote machine over count in Ward 1 & determine if there were discrepancies in other wards). Audit the September 2026 election to verify the # of voters who checked in is equal to the final machine vote tally for each ward. If there is a discrepancy that a manual count of the paper ballots be completed to ensure one vote per voter with no duplicate votes. (during the voting machine test this summer, it was observed that duplicate vote counts occurred when a ballot was accidentally re-entered & counted twice (ie when kicked out after being initially counted by the machine because there was a write in vote on the ballot). A written report of findings to ensure the integrity of our voting process be provided to the city council & the public. 56. Devine, Panitch – ORDERED: that the relevant provisions of Chapter 86, Traffic and Vehicles, be amended to provide that the intersection of Dwight Street and Maple Street southeast bound be designated No Right Turn On Red, and that a “No Turn On Red” sign be posted at that corner. Send to Ordinance, with a copy to the DPW and City Engineer. 57. Devine – ORDERED that the whenever the Building, Fire and Health Departments issue citations to businesses, if time allows to copy the City Council through our Administrative Assistant. 58. Devine – ORDERED that the Building and Health departments forward copies of the recent citations given to Motel 6 and the Budget Inn on Northampton Street to the City Council through our Administrative Assistant to be distributed to City Councilors. 59. Devine – ORDERED that the DPW paint a crosswalk on Hampden at Howard Street. 60. Live Spanish interpretation will be available on local access channel 15 using the television’s SAP option, through the live stream on the city website, as well as on the Zoom feed by clicking the interpretation option and choosing Spanish. Tuesday, October 6, 2026 6:30 PM AGENDA PRESIDENT’S REPORT PUBLIC HEARING PUBLIC COMMENT REGULAR AND PENDING EXECUTIVE SESSION MINUTES 1. June 11, 2024, September 4, 2024, and April 15, 2025 Executive Session Minutes – Reviewed and ready for partial release as of September 17, 2025 2. December 9, 2024 Finance Committee Executive Session Minutes – Reviewed and withheld in entirety as of September 17, 2025 3. From City Clerk Brenna Murphy Leary and Admin. Assistant Jeffery Anderson-Burgos- meeting minutes from September 15, 2026 LAID ON THE TABLE 4. Vacon- Greaney- ORDER: that city council go to the first ballot to elect a treasurer at the April 21, 2026 city council meeting in accordance with our current charter. Our city council appointed Collector has indicated interest in the Treasurer/Collector position. A majority of the city council has had the opportunity to interview our Collector. This appointment would legally establish the Treasurer position & for practical purposes combines the positions, while waiting for further charter changes that will be sent to the state legislature in a home rule petition. Transition changes can happen in coordination with other ordinance changes. COMMUNICATIONS 5. From Mayor Joshua Garcia-communication regarding the City Forestry Crew 6. From Mayor Joshua Garcia- letter appointing Mr. Stephen Fay of 218 Pleasant St. to serve as an alternate of the new Historical Commission. Mr. Fay’s term will expire on July 1, 2029. 7. From Mayor Joshua Garica-letter appointing Ms. Rebecca Lisi of 25 Reservation Rd. to serve on the Holyoke Redevelopment Authority. Ms. Lisi will replace Mr. Thomas Creed and will serve the remainder of his term, expiring November 1, 2026. 8. From Police Chief Brian Keenan-Policy and Procedure Automatic License Plate Recognition 9. From City of Holyoke Health Benefit Meeting Minutes July 15, 2026 10. From the Holyoke Redevelopment Authority-meeting minutes from June 17, July 15 and August 19, 2026. 11. From City Comptroller Sharon Bittner-Willis, FY2027 General Fund Expense YTD Report-Totals 12. From City Comptroller Sharon Bittner-Willis, FY2027 Sewer Enterprise Expense YTD Report-Totals 13. Petition from various residents regarding voting against cancelling Columbus Day PETITIONS 14. Petition from Roxanne Roman of 76 Elmwood Ave for a zone change from RA to R-2 to develop two duplexes on the vacant parcel 15. Petition from Daphine Nyachowe or 601 Northampton St for a Livery License 16. Petition from Carlos Colon for a Street Vendor License at 920 Main St. for a food truck REPORTS OF COMMITTEES 17. The Committee on Ordinance to whom was referred a Zone change application from BG (business general) to DR (downtown residential) of Irfan Raheel at 172 Sargeant Street (060-06-001) to allow for second floor residential use. Recommended that the zone change be granted. 18. The Committee on Ordinance to whom was referred an order that the Honorable City Council review the ordinance that establishes the operating time frames for cannabis dispensaries. Recommended that the order be adopted. 19. The Committee on Ordinance to whom was referred an order that ordinance sections 2-38 and 2-39 be revised to replace “Columbus Day” with “Indigenous Peoples’ Day.” Recommended that the order be adopted. 20. The Committee on Ordinance to whom was referred an order that the DPW install a Handicap Sign for Luis Davila of 240 Walnut St. #PL8720803 Recommended that the order be adopted. 21. The Committee on Ordinance to whom was referred an order that the handicap parking sign located at 107 Brown Ave be removed as the tenant who originally requested and utilized it has moved and the space is no longer needed. Recommended that the order be adopted. 22. The Committee on Ordinance to whom was referred an order that the City Council review Holyoke’s municipal rules, ordinances, and any related materials that may be discovered during the process of review, relatiing to notices to citizens of proposed changes in the Zoning Ordinance and publication of such notices, and make such amendments to our ordinances and rules that may be found desirable in light of that review. While required notices are set forth in state law, a review of our local ordinances, etc., may reveal inefficiencies that are not required by said state law. This order is intended to be broadly construed to cover any public notice requirements, with respect to any other matters, that may be found to be affected by such municipal rules or ordinances. Recommended that the order has been complied with. 23. The Committee on Ordinance to whom was referred an order that any person who is a realtor or owns a real estate business who is appointed by the Mayor to the Planning Board and confirmed by the City Council SHALL recuse themselves from any zoning vote that would enrich them or their business unless they receive written approval from the State Conflict of Interest department. Recommended that the order has been complied with. 24. The Committee on Ordinance to whom was referred an order that the Planning Board be invited to appear in person if possible to the September meeting of the Ordinance Committee. Recommended that the order has been complied with. 25. The Committee on Ordinance to whom was referred an order that Council make the necessary zoning ordinance changes in order for us to clarify parking on residential properties and create an enforcement structure. Recommended that the order be given a leave to withdraw. 26. The Committee on Ordinance to whom was referred a Petition of Paola M. Rosado Freytiz of 71 Brown Ave Apt 1 for street vendor license for food truck at 1810 Northampton Street. Awaiting disposition 27. The Committee on Ordinance to whom was referred an order that the Ordinance Committee increase the fines for any and all ordinances dealing with blocking driveways, crosswalks and parking too close to intersections, and any other citable offenses listed on the attached sample parking ticket. Fines shall be increased to $75 and up to $150. Any violation of the parking ban shall be a fine of $150. In addition, if warranted, a payment plan may be implemented for low income and elderly residents. Awaiting disposition 28. The Committee on Ordinance to whom was referred an order that the fines be increased for illegal dumping, especially construction equipment and garbage on a sidewalk or street that has not been recycled. The word “rubbish” shall mean solid waste consisting of both combustible and non combustible wastes such as paper, wrappings, newsprint, cardboard, tin cans, yard clippings, leaves, glass, plastics (as in nip bottles) and bedding. Awaiting disposition 29. The Committee on Ordinance to whom was referred an order that the Sound Permitting Ordinance be amended to designate the License Board as the granting authority for sound permits, rather than the Chief of Police. This change is intended to align the permitting process with the License Board’s established role in reviewing, issuing, and regulating licenses, while ensuring a transparent, consistent, and civilian-led decision-making process. Transferring this authority would provide clearer standards, improved accountability, and greater procedural fairness for applicants, while allowing the Police Department to focus on enforcement and public safety responsibilities rather than administrative permitting functions. Awaiting disposition 30. The Committee on Ordinance to whom was referred an order that the City Council review Section 38-71 of the Holyoke Code of Ordinances and amend it as necessary to remove outdated exemptions therein. Awaiting disposition 31. The Committee on Ordinance to whom was referred an order The city council amend chapter 86 of the city’s ordinances (and elsewhere if so deemed) to allow two-wheeled vehicles (i.e. motorcycles) to park multiple like-sized vehicles in any single public parking space as the City Engineer may determine (potentially up to three) whether metered or not metered. This shall be applicable to parking spaces in city-owned parking garages including Mayor Taupier and Mayor Proulx. The city shall allow private parking lots the option to institute a similar parking schedule for motorcycles and like-sized vehicles. Alternatively, the city allow said right to be permitted by special permit issued by the Chief of Police if other traffic standards do not allow this ordinance change. City Council consider adoption of chapter 40, section 22 of MGL. Awaiting disposition 32. The Committee on Ordinance to whom was referred an order That an ordinance be created that will require an annual registration, liability insurance and an official Massachusetts license plate for high speed motorized bicycles. Awaiting disposition 33. The Committee on Ordinance to whom was referred an order That regulations be created through the Holyoke Police Department and/or an ordinance be created in accordance with MGL c90, s 1E as it relates to as “pocket bikes”, “mini bikes”, “mini motorcycles”, “motorized skateboards” and any other two-wheeled tandem or three-wheeled devices, that has handlebars, designed to be stood or sat upon by the operator, powered by an electric or gas powered motor that is capable or propelling the device with or without human propulsion, and is not defined as a motor vehicle or motorcycle under the law of the Commonwealth of Massachusetts, shall be considered as a “motorized scooter”. Awaiting disposition 34. The Committee on Ordinance to whom was referred an order that the City Council amend City Ordinance 6-2 Drinking Alcoholic Beverage on Public Street, Section (a) changed to include the following wording. “The drinking of alcoholic beverages by any persons while, upon any way or in any place to which the public has a right of access, or upon any way or in any place to which members of the public have access as invitees or licensees” Awaiting disposition 35. The Committee on Ordinance to whom was referred an order that the City change the use of the lot at the corner of Adam and South Summer from being a 24hr parking to a Residential Parking from 5pm to 7am. Morgan School Staff Parking from 7am- 5pm. Awaiting disposition 36. The Committee on Ordinance to whom was referred an order that 2 lanes from Linden Street onto Beech Street be designated as a left turn lane and a right turn lane and painted with the appropriate turn arrows. Awaiting disposition 37. The Committee on Ordinance to whom was referred an order that a crosswalk be added across Northampton Street at River Terrace. Awaiting disposition 38. The Committee on Ordinance to whom was referred an order that a crosswalk be added across Hampton Knolls where it intersects with Northampton Street. Awaiting disposition 39. The Committee on Ordinance to whom was referred an order that Sec. 54-18. on removal of shopping carts be revised to add that establishments who employ shopping carts must ensure that a locking wheel system is used and that businesses have a responsibility to maintain them/handle removal of carts. Review and revise the existing enforcement structure for carts found off property. Awaiting disposition 40. The Committee on Ordinance to whom was referred an order that the Clerk and the Law Department draft a list of ordinances that they have a record of being changed in the past that were never presented to Municode and thus not in the current “Adopted Ordinances Not Yet Codified” queue. Awaiting disposition 41. The Committee on Ordinance to whom was referred an order that our winter parking ordinance be revised as necessary for clarity, functionality, and flexibility based on constituent and DPW needs. Awaiting disposition 42. The Committee on Ordinance to whom was referred an order that sections 2-35 (b) (i), (ii), and (iv) of the code of ordinances be deleted to allow for hiring new employees above the mid range. Awaiting disposition 43. The Committee on Ordinance to whom was referred an order that the City Council President establish by ordinance a temporary ad-hoc committee to expire/sunset by June 30, 2027 to study and provide an analysis on the potential impacts of commercial data center development in Holyoke, including electrical demand, water consumption, environmental impacts, tax revenue, economic development opportunities, zoning considerations, public safety concerns, and best practices adopted by other municipalities, and to make recommendations to the City Council regarding potential zoning and permitting requirements. This Ad-Hoc Committee shall include one member from: Holyoke Gas and Electric Holyoke Water Works or Member of Water Commission Massachusetts Green High-Performing Computing Center Planning Board Conservation Commission Office of Planning and Development Community Member or Resident appointed by the City Council President City Council Awaiting disposition 44. The Committee on Ordinance to whom was referred an order that in accordance with Section 86-95 of the Holyoke Code of Ordinances, 90 degree diagonal parking be established on the southerly side of Westfield Road at the 224 Westfield Rd property beginning at a point approximately 510 feet easterly of Bray Park Drive to a point 85 feet farther east. Awaiting disposition 45. The Committee on Public Safety to whom was referred an order Invite Veterans Services Department Director Laddy Rua to an upcoming Public Safety meeting for a conversation highlighting the services they provide and render in Holyoke to support veterans, especially those dealing with Post-Traumatic Stress Disorder (PTSD). Recommended that the order has been complied with. 46. The Committee on Public Safety to whom was referred an order Invite the Holyoke Safe Neighborhood Initiative to an upcoming Public Safety meeting for a conversation highlighting the work that they are doing in Holyoke to create safe, healthy & economically viable neighborhoods through information sharing, identifying at-risk youth, referrals and community efforts. Recommended that the order has been complied with. 47. The Committee on Public Safety to whom was referred an order that city council takes steps to support neighborhoods who wish to establish a neighborhood watch to help prevent crime. Recommended that the order has been complied with. 48. The Committee on Public Safety to whom was referred an order that the City Council review the history, authorization, and all aspects of the use of Flock cameras in Holyoke, and of any other automated license plate technology (ALPR) that may be deployed or under consideration for deployment, in order to determine whether legislation is necessary to address any civil rights and privacy issues that may be implicated by the presence of this technology and to enact such legislation should it prove to be needed. The information needed for this review shall include but not be limited to the city’s contract with Flock, including details of any amendments thereto; information showing who authorized the installation and when, for what reasons; how much the contract costs the city and where it is in the budget; where the data from these ALPRs is or may be shared or queried; for how long it is preserved; how it is safeguarded from abuse and access for improper purposes or by unauthorized persons; and whether Holyoke’s and Flock’s terms and practices are in compliance with Massachusetts law regarding the sharing of data, particularly with federal agencies. The Holyoke Police Department and the Law Department are requested to provide all relevant data to the City Council to assist in this review. Recommended that the order has been complied with. 49. The Committee on Public Safety to whom was referred an order The City of Holyoke prohibit the use of GLOVE (Generated Low Output Voltage Emitter) gloves. Classified as a CD3 (conductive distraction and de-escalation device), these devices work differently from other incapacitation devices (stun guns, tasers) by shocking the skin to cause neuro-peripheral disruption rather than using probe projectiles or higher voltage neuro-muscular disruption. In other words, it inflicts localized pain on subjects in order to enforce compliance rather than muscular disruption provided by other devices. Recommended that the order has been complied with. 50. The Committee on Charter and Rules to whom was referred an order : That a new City Council rule be enacted as follows: During a City Council meeting if a councilor wants to take up an agenda item out of order that whenever possible let the President know PRIOR to the item being taken out of order. Recommended that the order be given a leave to withdraw. MOTIONS, ORDERS AND RESOLUTIONS 51. Vacon- ORDER: That Columbus Day & Indigenous People Day be named together in our ordinance. 52. Vacon- ORDER: When a legal notice is sent to citizens for a zone change, a summary explaining the effect of & rationale for the change, (similar to a ballot question summary) is provided with the notice. 53. Vacon- ORDER: that our auditor submit the audit plan as previously voted by the city council and appear at Finance Committee to present the audit plan. Send to Finance Committee & Auditor. 54. Vacon- ORDER: request the Board of Health to provide a report on the status of removal of kratom products from all stores in accordance with the statewide ban in effect as of 8/26226. 55. Vacon- ORDER: The Board of Registrars/City Clerk audit the November 2025 votes (to determine the cause of a 6 vote machine over count in Ward 1 & determine if there were discrepancies in other wards). Audit the September 2026 election to verify the # of voters who checked in is equal to the final machine vote tally for each ward. If there is a discrepancy that a manual count of the paper ballots be completed to ensure one vote per voter with no duplicate votes. (during the voting machine test this summer, it was observed that duplicate vote counts occurred when a ballot was accidentally re-entered & counted twice (ie when kicked out after being initially counted by the machine because there was a write in vote on the ballot). A written report of findings to ensure the integrity of our voting process be provided to the city council & the public. 56. Devine, Panitch – ORDERED: that the relevant provisions of Chapter 86, Traffic and Vehicles, be amended to provide that the intersection of Dwight Street and Maple Street southeast bound be designated No Right Turn On Red, and that a “No Turn On Red” sign be posted at that corner. Send to Ordinance, with a copy to the DPW and City Engineer. 57. Devine – ORDERED that the whenever the Building, Fire and Health Departments issue citations to businesses, if time allows to copy the City Council through our Administrative Assistant. 58. Devine – ORDERED that the Building and Health departments forward copies of the recent citations given to Motel 6 and the Budget Inn on Northampton Street to the City Council through our Administrative Assistant to be distributed to City Councilors. 59. Devine – ORDERED that the DPW paint a crosswalk on Hampden at Howard Street. 60. DEVINE – Ordered, that the amount of THREE THOUSAND SIX HUNDRED FIFTY-EIGHT AND 72/100 DOLLARS ($3,658.72) be authorized from the WAR

ARTICLE 9. TOWN GENERAL BYLAWS: PROHIBITION OF UNAPPROVED CAMPING AND TEMPORARY STRUCTURES ON MUNICIPAL PROPERTY § 1. Purpose and Intent This Bylaw is enacted to protect the health, safety, and general welfare of the public; to prevent environmental degradation, forest fires, and soil erosion; and to preserve municipal parks, recreation fields, public grounds, and protected conservation lands for the safe, intended enjoyment of all residents. § 2. Definitions « "Camping" means the use of Town property for temporary living or overnight habitation purposes, including but not limited to: erecting or pitching tents, tarpaulins, lean-tos, shanties, or other temporary shelters; establishing a campsite; sleeping overnight; or utilizing sleeping gear, cots, hammocks, or motor vehicles for living quarters. * "Camp Paraphernalia" includes, but is not limited to, tarps, cots, beds, sleeping bags, cooking equipment, open flame stoves, portable generators, and improvised sanitary facilities. ¢ "Town Property" means all land, conservation areas, forests, public parks, athletic fields, historic sites, facility grounds, rights-of-way, municipal parking areas, and open spaces owned, leased, managed, or controlled by the Town. § 3. Prohibitions e Unapproved Camping: No person shall camp, establish living quarters, or erect any temporary shelter on Town Property at any time, whether between sunset and sunrise or for continuous habitation during daylight hours. e Unauthorized Fires: No person shall ignite, build, or maintain a campfire, bon fire, or portable fuel burner on Town Property without a written permit issued by the Fire Department and, where applicable, the Conservation Commission. 8 4. Exemptions The prohibitions of this Bylaw shall not apply to: 1. Town-sponsored recreational events or emergency management operations explicitly authorized by the Town Administrator or Select Board. 2. Controlled events, such as scout campouts, that have obtained a formal, written permit from the Conservation Commission (for conservation properties) or the Select Board (for general town grounds) at least 14 business days prior to the event. 3. Law enforcement, fire, or public works personnel engaged in official duties. § 5. Enforcement and Penalties « Enforcing Agents: This Bylaw shall be enforced by the Police Department, the Conservation Agent, or any designated Town Code Enforcement Officer. Order to Vacate: Any enforcing agent may issue a verbal or written order to any person violating this Bylaw to immediately cease camping, dismantle shelters, extinguish fires, and vacate the property within a designated timeframe, not to exceed two (2) hours. Non-Criminal Disposition: Violations of this Bylaw may be penalized through non- criminal disposition pursuant to M.G.L. c. 40, § 21D. Penalties shall be assessed as follows: o First Offense: Written Warning and Order to Vacate. o Second Offense: $100.00 fine. o Third and Subsequent Offenses: $300.00 fine per day of continued violation. § 6. Impoundment of Unattended Property Any camp paraphernalia or temporary structures left unattended on Town Property in violation of this Bylaw may be removed and impounded by the Town 24 hours after a written notice of violation is posted on or near the items. Items presenting an immediate environmental, sanitary, or fire hazard may be removed immediately. § 7. Severability If any section, sentence, or clause of this Bylaw is deemed invalid bya court of competent jurisdiction, the remaining provisions shall remain in full force and effect. ARTICLE 10. TOWN GENERAL BYLAWS: PROHIBITION OF OVERNIGHT PARKING ON CONSERVATION PROPERTY § 1. Purpose and Authority This Bylaw is adopted pursuant to M.G.L. c. 40, $21 and M.G.L. c. 40, § 8C to protect public safety, prevent illegal dumping, mitigate fire risk, and preserve public access to town-owned conservation lands, trailheads, and adjacent access roads. § 2. Definitions “Conservation Property" means all land, trailheads, parking areas, access roads, and rights-of-way under the care, custody, management, or control of the Conservation Commission. "Motor Vehicle" means any passenger vehicle, truck, motorcycle, all-terrain vehicle, camper, recreational vehicle (RV), trailer, or towed unit. “Overnight Hours” means the period between 10:00 PM and 5:00 AM daily, or between one-half hour after sunset and one-half hour before sunrise where posted. § 3. Prohibitions Unauthorized Overnight Parking: No person shall park, leave standing, or store any Motor Vehicle on Conservation Property during Overnight Hours. Continuous Staging: Leaving an unattached trailer, recreational vehicle, or unregistered motor vehicle on Conservation Property for more than twenty-four (24) consecutive hours is prohibited at all times. § 4. Exemptions This Bylaw shall not apply to: 1. 2. Emergency vehicles, police cruisers, or public works equipment engaged in official duties. Town personnel, contractors, or Conservation Commission agents conducting site maintenance, natural resource management, or emergency repairs. Individuals who have obtained prior written authorization from the Conservation Commission or Police Department at least forty-eight (48) hours in advance for sanctioned municipal or research activities. § 5. Enforcement and Towing Authority e Enforcing Officers: This Bylaw shall be enforced by any Police Officer, the Conservation Agent, or designated municipal Code Enforcement Officers. * Towing Authority: Any Motor Vehicle parked in violation of this Bylaw may be immediately towed and impounded at the vehicle owner’s sole expense pursuant to M.G.L. c. 266, § 120D. « Required Signage: The Conservation Commission shall ensure conspicuous signage stating “NO OVERNIGHT PARKING - TOW ZONE — BYLAW ART. [XX]" is posted at all primary trailhead parking areas and access points. § 6. Penalties Violations of this Bylaw may be enforced through non-criminal disposition pursuant to M.G.L. c. 40, § 21D. Each calendar day a violation continues shall constitute a separate offense. e First Offense: $50.00 fine. * Second Offense: $100.00 fine. e Third and Subsequent Offenses: $250.00 fine per day, plus all applicable towing and storage fees. § 7. Severability If any section, sentence, or clause of this Bylaw is held invalid by a court of competent jurisdiction, the remaining provisions shall remain in full force and effect. ARTICLE 11. ZONING BYLAW ARTICLES REVISIONS TO SECTIONS 2.32, 4.2, 4.9, 4.10, 4.12, 10.1, AND 10.4 TO CONFORM THE ZONING BYLAW TO AMENDMENTS TO THE ZONING ACT, G.L. c. 40A (Two-thirds vote required) To see if the Town will vote to amend the Hubbardston Zoning Bylaws Sections 2.32, 4.2, 4.9, 4.10, 4.11, 4.12, 10.1, 10.4, and 17.9 by adding the following language in bold italics, deleting the language shown struck through, and further that non-substantive changes to the numbering of the Zoning Bylaw be permitted in order that it be in compliance with the numbering format of the Zoning Bylaw; 2.32 Variance. An extraordinary remedy which may be granted by the Board of Appeals if it finds that owing to circumstances relating to soil conditions; topography; lot size, frontage, or setback requirements, a literal enforcement of these zoning bylaws or a special permit will create a suibstantiat hardship practical difficulty and that granting of a variance will not adversely affect the land use and environmental objectives of these zoning bylaws, as set forth in Article 10 and G.L. c. 40A, § 10. 4.2 Uses Permitted By Special Permit in Residential Districts. g. Additions and/or alterations to existing non-conforming structure or use, except where such addition or alteration is permitted as of right under Section 4.9.B. 4.9 Existing Uses Continued (Grandfathering). Any structures or uses lawfully existing on the effective date of these zoning bylaws and lawfully existing uses which will become non-conforming uses on the effective date of these bylaws may be continued in accordance with the provisions of General Laws Chapter 40A, Section 6, Structural additions to pre-existing, non-conforming structures, or structure being used by pre-existing non-conforming uses, can be expanded up to 50% greater in size than the size of such structure at the time of the adoption of this bylaw, except as provided in Subsection B below. Any Except for an extension or alteration permitted as of right under Subsection B below, any subsequent and substantial alteration, or extension of anon- conforming use must be authorized by special permit issued by the Planning Board which will be granted only if the Board finds that the proposed alteration, reconstruction, or extension will not be substantially more detrimental to the neighborhood than is the existing non-conforming use. A. Except for an extension or alteration permitted as of right under Subsection B below, “A non-conforming building or structure may be altered or enlarged provided that such alteration or enlargement conforms to applicable yard, building height and lot coverage requirements, but no non-conforming structure shall be permitted unless there is a finding by the Special Permit Granting Authority that such change, extension, or alteration shall not be substantially more detrimental than the existing non-conforming use to the neighborhood”. Notwithstanding Subsection A above and notwithstanding any other provision of these zoning bylaws requiring a special permit or a finding, pre-existing non-conforming structures that do not conform to these zoning bylaws because of lot size or shape, frontage, lot coverage or floor area ratio requirements may be extended or altered as of right, without a special permit and without the need fora finding by the Special Permit Granting Authority, if such extension or alteration complies with the current dimensional regulations of these zoning bylaws regarding height, stories and setback, as provided by G.L. c. 40A, § 6. 4.10 Abandonment of a Non-Conforming Use.
