ARTICLE 1 – Transfer Increased State Aid to Ipswich Public Schools Submitted By: School Department To see if the Town will vote to supplement the FY2027 School Budget approved under Article 4 at the May 12, 2026 Annual Town Meeting by appropriating the additional sum of $131,463; or take any other action relative thereto. Summary: The FY2027 State budget has been finalized, and the Town will receive additional State Aid through its education funding accounts; primarily, Chapter 70 funding. These funds will be used to offset the cost of school expenses. Requires a Simple Majority Vote. ARTICLE 2 – Capital Stabilization Fund Transfer for School Projects Submitted By: School Department To see if the Town will vote to transfer from the Capital Stabilization Fund the sum of $240,000 to support the following critical improvements needed at the Winthrop Elementary School; or take any action relative thereto.        Univent upgrades for air handling (air quality, health) - $100,000 Kitchen equipment upgrades and replacements (food preparation) - $8,350 Exhaust fan replacements (air quality, health) - $10,000 Exterior metal door replacements (building security) - $25,000 Suspended ceiling replacements (only as needed for safety, conditions) - $26,650 Insulation wrap on all boiler pipes (energy conservation) - $10,000 Window repairs and replacements (building security and energy conservation) - $60,000 Summary: At the Annual Town Meeting on May 13,2025 the Town approved $240,000 in capital funding for a modular classroom building for the Winthrop Elementary School. As final project costs came in over the summer 2025 it was realized that there was insufficient funding to support the costs of site work, utilities, design, construction, and installation, forcing the project to be halted. Since that time, with the appropriate and necessary reorganization of classrooms and learning spaces at the Winthrop School, it has also been determined that a modular building on the Winthrop School campus is not necessary at this time. However, other critical building safety, security, and capital equipment needs exist at the Winthrop School and the School Department is requesting that the funds originally approved for the modular classroom building, which were ultimately deposited into the Capital Stabilization Fund, be repurposed to meet the other capital needs at the Winthrop School. These other, more critical needs include HVAC air handling, exterior door repairs and replacements, flooring maintenance equipment, and selected ceiling and window repairs and replacements. Requires a Simple Majority Vote. ARTICLE 3 – Appropriation to Essex Tech Submitted By: Town Manager To see if the Town will vote to modify the amount appropriated under Article 6 at the May 12, 2026 Annual Town Meeting by reducing or increasing the Town’s share of the budget for the FY2027 annual operating budget and debt service expenses of the Essex North Shore Agricultural & Technical School District; or take any action relative thereto. Summary: The Essex North Shore Agricultural & Technical School District Estimated FY27 Budget was voted at the Annual Town Meeting in the amount of $416,000 for the estimated tuition and transportation costs for 15 students. After October 1st, official enrollment will be complete and the final budget figure will be available. The final FY2027 Budget figure will be included in the motion of this article. Requires a Simple Majority Vote. ARTICLE 4 - Amend Definition of “Structure” – Ipswich Protective Zoning Bylaw Submitted By: Planning Board To see if the Town will vote to amend the Ipswich Protective Zoning Bylaw by revising Section III, Definitions, to update the definition of “Structure” as set forth below; or take any action relative thereto. [Note: Strikethrough = Language to be Deleted / Bold Italics = New Language] STRUCTURE: Any constructed, erected, or placed material or combination of materials in or upon the ground to give support or shelter, including, but not limited to, buildings, mobile homes, radio towers, sheds, signs and storage bins, swimming pools, tennis courts, platforms, and fences., and intended for permanence, or attachment and/or anchoring to something intended for permanence. The word "structure" shall be construed where the context allows as though followed by the words "or part thereof.” Summary: The Director of Planning & Development and the Ipswich Building Commissioner/Code Enforcement Officer propose the amendment to the definition of “Structure” in order to provide a more fundamental, comprehensive, understandable, and defensible codification of the meaning of a “Structure” for municipal land-use regulatory review and permitting processes. Requires a Two-Thirds Majority Vote. ARTICLE 5 - Amend Definition of “Residential Mixed Use” – Ipswich Protective Zoning Bylaw Submitted By: Planning Board To see if the Town will vote to amend the Ipswich Protective Zoning Bylaw by revising Section III, Definitions, to update the definition of “Use, Residential Mixed” as set forth below; or take any action relative thereto. [Note: Strikethrough = Language to be Deleted / Bold Italics = New Language] VI: Protective Zoning Bylaw – Article III. Definitions Item: “Use, Residential-Mixed” USE, RESIDENTIAL-MIXED: A building which contains two or more principal uses, at least one of which is residential, and at least one of which is non-residential and located on the ground floor. The nonresidential use shall occupy no less than twenty-five percent (25%) of the building’s ground floor, and shall be located within the front facade of the building, so as to be oriented to, and facing the front sidewalk and/or street. The principal uses in a Residential Mixed-Use building shall be subject to all applicable regulations and conditions in this Zoning Bylaw for those individual uses, including the Dimensional and Density Regulations in Section VI, if this use is not specifically mentioned in Section VI. (Added by 10/25/16 STM; approved by AG 2/14/17) (Amended by 10/17/20 STM; approved by AG 3/18/21) Summary: The Director of Planning & Development proposes the amendment to the definition of “Use, Residential Mixed” in order to provide the addition of a regulatory permitting requirement that specifies in a mixed-use building, the non-residential use shall occupy no less than 25% of the building’s ground floor and be located in the front façade of the building, in order to assure socially & economically and functionally vital, vibrant, safe, healthy, and traditional mixed-use streets and districts. Requires a Two-Thirds Majority Vote. ARTICLE 6 - Accessory Dwelling Unit (ADU) Bylaw Amendments – Ipswich Protective Zoning Bylaw Submitted By: Planning Board & Building Department To see if the Town will vote to amend the Town of Ipswich Protective Zoning Bylaw by (1) deleting Section IX.J Accessory Apartments, (2) deleting Section IX P. Conversion of Accessory Buildings into Residential Units, (3) deleting Section IX.U Detached Accessory Units, (4) adding new provision Section IX.U – Protected Use Accessory Dwelling Unit (5) amending the other provisions of the Ipswich Protective Zoning Bylaw to be consistent with these changes, all as set forth below; or take any action relative thereto. [Note: Strikethrough = Language to be Deleted / Bold Italics = New Language] Town of Ipswich Protective Zoning Bylaw: TABLE OF CONTENTS Section IX Special Regulations J. (Formerly) Accessory Apartment…98 P. (Formerly) Conversion of Accessory Building into Residential Unit …113 U. Detached Protected Use Accessory Dwelling Units…127 SECTION III: DEFINITIONS ACCESSORY APARTMENT: A separate dwelling unit within a single-family dwelling that is a subordinate part of the single-family dwelling and complies with the requirements of IX.J. of this zoning bylaw. (Added by 4/5/99 Special Town Meeting; approved by Attorney General 8/2/99) (Amended by 10/18/04 Special Town Meeting; approved by Attorney General 1/27/05) Any Accessory Apartment (Formerly Section IX. J) for which a special permit was issued by the Zoning Board of Appeals prior to the enactment of M.G.L. c. 40A, § 3, ¶ 11 and 760 CMR 71. See Section IX. U. Protected Use Accessory Dwelling Unit of this bylaw. BASEMENT: The floor of a building which is partly or entirely below ground level. Basements shall be considered a story only if it meets the definition of ‘story above grade plane’ (see "story above grade plane"). CONVERSION OF ACCESSORY BUILDING INTO RESIDENTIAL UNIT: Any Conversion of Accessory Building into Residential Unit (Formerly Section IX. P) for which a special permit was issued by the Planning Board prior to the enactment of M.G.L. c. 40A, § 3, ¶ 11 and 760 CMR 71. See Section IX. U. Protected Use Accessory Dwelling Unit of this bylaw. CRAWLSPACE: An enclosed underfloor or roof space with a minimum height of at least 18 inches that provides access for inspection, maintenance or utility purposes only. DETACHED ACCESSORY DWELLING UNIT: Any Detached Accessory Dwelling Unit for which a special permit was issued by the Planning Board prior to the enactment of M.G.L. c. 40A, § 3, ¶ 11 and 760 CMR 71. See Revised Section IX. U. Protected Use Accessory Dwelling Unit of this bylaw. GRADE PLANE: A reference plane representing the average of finished ground level adjoining the building at exterior walls. Where the finished ground level slopes away from the exterior walls, the reference plane shall be established by the lowest points within the area between the building and the lot line or where the lot line is more than 6 feet from the building, the point 6 feet from the building shall be used in the reference plane averaging. GROSS FLOOR AREA (GFA) FOR PADUs ONLY. The sum of the areas of all stories of the building of compliant ceiling height pursuant to the Building Code, including full basements, lofts, and intermediate floored tiers, measured from the interior faces of exterior walls or from the centerline of walls separating buildings or dwelling units but excluding crawl spaces, garage parking areas, attics, enclosed porches and similar spaces. Where there are multiple Principal Dwellings on the Lot, the GFA of the largest Principal Dwelling shall be used for determining the maximum size of a Protected Use ADU and when there is a multi-unit Principal Dwelling on the Lot, the combined total of the units shall be used for determining the maximum size of a PADU. PRINCIPAL DWELLING A structure that contains at least one Dwelling Unit and is, or will be, located on the same Lot as a PADU. A structure can qualify as a Principal Dwelling under this Section IX.U regardless of whether it, or the Lot on which it is situated, conforms to zoning. PROTECTED USE ACCESSORY DWELLING UNIT (PADU). A self-contained housing unit, inclusive of sleeping, cooking and sanitary facilities on the same Lot as a Principal Dwelling in a Single-family Residential Zoning District (as defined in 760 CMR 71.00) that: a.) maintains a separate entrance, either directly from the outside or through an entry hall or corridor shared with the Principal Dwelling sufficient to meet the requirements of the Building Code for safe egress; b.) is not larger in Gross Floor Area than ½ the Gross Floor Area of the Principal Dwelling or 900 square feet, whichever is smaller. Only one (1) accessory dwelling unit on a lot may qualify as a PADU. An accessory dwelling unit that is nonconforming to Zoning shall still qualify as a PADU if it otherwise meets this definition. STORY: That portion of a building between the upper surface of a floor and the upper surface of the floor or roof next above. Basements shall be considered a story if it meets the definition of ‘story above grade plane’. as defined in the State Building Code. STORY ABOVE GRADE PLANE: Any story having its finished floor surface entirely above grade plane (see “grade plane”), or in which the finished surface of the floor next above is:   More than 6 feet (1829 mm) above grade plane average; or More than 12 feet (3658 mm) above the finished ground level at any point. SECTION V. USE REGULATIONS: FOOTNOTES TO USE REGULATIONS: Footnote #19. Residential units in an Assisted Living or Life Care Facility, regardless of whether they are single-family, two-family, or multi-family dwelling units, with the exception of one (1) PADU per Lot (where allowed), are subject to the same Inclusionary Housing Requirements that apply to multi-family residential developments, as described in Section IX.I.3.a. of this zoning bylaw. (Amended by 10/15/07 STM; approved by AG 1/23/08) (Amended by 10/20/08 STM; approved by AG 1/28/09) Footnote #20. Multi-family residential developments, with the exception of one (1) Protected Use Accessory Dwelling Unit per Lot (where allowed), are subject to the Inclusionary Housing Requirements in Section IX.I. of this zoning bylaw. (Added by 10/20/97 STM; approved by AG 2/10/98) (Amended by 10/21/02 STM; approved by AG 2/3/03) Footnote #30. Any expansion of or alteration to an existing two-family dwelling, a multi-family dwelling, or a multi-family residential development, whether said use is conforming or nonconforming, that creates one (1) or more additional residential dwelling units, except where such additional dwelling unit is the one allowable PADU on the subject lot, shall require a special permit from the Planning Board. (Added by 10/19/09 STM; approved by AG 2/16/10) SECTION VI. DIMENSIONAL AND DENSITY REGULATIONS B. Table of Dimensional and Density Regulations (See edits to Table B. below). F. Requirements for Accessory Buildings and Structures 1. An accessory building or structure may be located in accordance with the Table of Dimensional and Density Regulations (Accessory Buildings and Structures) and Footnote #2 to said Table. 2. An accessory buildings and or structures other than a PADU shall be located on the same lot as the a principal building or use provided that not more than twenty-five percent (25%) of a minimum lot area shall be so occupied and, further, that an accessory building or structure shall not be located less than five (5) feet from the principal building. 3. Except for PADUs as defined in Section IX. U. of this bylaw, accessory buildings and structures are prohibited from having attached decks or porches or other similar structures unless the accessory building or structure is used for habitation, and provided that the deck or porch or other similar structure is no more than sixty-four (64) square feet in size and open to the sky. 4. Except for PADUs as defined in Section IX. U. of this bylaw, buildings and structures used for agricultural purposes as defined by M.G. L., C.40A, s.3. accessory buildings and structures greater than one thousand (1000) seven hundred fifty (750) square feet in area or more than twenty-five (25) feet in height, and located on lots less than five acres in size in the residential districts, shall be allowed only by special permit from the Zoning Board of Appeals, and only upon a finding that: a. 1. The proposed accessory structure satisfies the criteria for Special Permit as prescribed in Section XI.J.2., paragraphs a. and b. of this bylaw; and b. 2. The proposed accessory structure does not create a substantially greater burden for the Town or neighborhood than would an accessory structure under seven hundred and fifty (750) one thousand (1000) square feet in area or under twenty-five (25) feet in height. Considerations include: i. Whether the traffic generation and/or parking needs associated with the proposed accessory structure would be detrimental to the surrounding neighborhood; ii. Whether the proposed accessory structure requires extension or alteration of existing utilities that would otherwise be adequate for a smaller accessory structure; iii. Whether the large size of the proposed accessory structure necessitates design, construction, or other physical features out of character for the district that could be avoided with a smaller accessory structure; and iv. Whether the design of the proposed accessory structure, in terms of materials, proportions, height, architectural details and scale, is adequate to ensure that the large accessory structure preserves the character of the surrounding area and is compatible with the architectural design style of the principal building on the site; and v. Whether the proposed accessory structure produces or exacerbates any other impact that the SPGA deems a detriment to public health, safety, and welfare which could be avoided with a smaller accessory structure; and 5. 3. The principal use to which the proposed structure will be accessory is permitted in the zoning district as a matter of right, as prescribed in Section V.D. TABLE OF USE REGULATIONS and the lot and principal structure conforms to all dimensional and density regulations of Section VI. of this zoning bylaw. 6. Accessory structures that are tent-like, made of canvas or similar materials, and greater than 120 square feet in area, shall be allowed only by special permit from the Zoning Board of Appeals except for those structures that are for temporary purposes only. VI. SELECT BOARD COMMENTS / TOWN ADMINSTRATOR ANNOUNCEMENTS a. Next Select Board Meeting will be on 10/26/26. VII. EXECUTIVE SESSION a. Motion to enter into Executive Session (not to reconvene in open session) under G.L. c.30A, Section 21 (a) (2): To conduct strategy sessions related to non-union personnel, not to reconvene in open session. VIII. ADJOURNMENT Rules of Procedure for Board Meetings of Lanesborough Select Board Meetings I. AGENDA A. The Town Administrative Assistant, in consultation with the Town Administrator and Chairman of the Select Board shall prepare an Agenda for the Select Board meetings. B. Any requests for matters to be placed on the agenda shall be submitted in writing to the Town Administrative Assistant by noon three business days prior to regularly scheduled meetings. Anyone requesting items be placed on the agenda shall provide the topic of the item and sufficient information and detail so as to provide a reasonable notice of the nature and purpose of the agenda item. C. Agendas will be posted a minimum of 48 hours in advance of any meeting on our Town website and Town bulletin board. D. Those wishing to speak in the public comment portion of the agenda shall provide their name and the topic of their comment. Topics shall be limited to matters of concern, official action or deliberation which are or may be before the Select Board. II. MEETINGS A. Public Notice of the meetings shall be advertised and posted by the Administrative Assistant as required by law. B. The Chairman of the Select Board shall direct the meeting. In the absence of the Chairman, the senior member of the Select Board shall direct the meeting and shall have all powers and duties of the Chairman. C. The Modern Rules of Order shall be used to conduct the meeting unless otherwise modified by these Rules or altered by the Select Board. The Lanesborough Select Board shall be addressed by their respective titles. D. Residents and/or taxpayers may use audio or stenographic recorders to record all or any portion of the meeting. Said recorders shall be operated from the area set aside for the general public seating and may not be placed on the Select Board’s table without prior consent of the Chairman. E. Video recorders may be used to record all or any portion of a public meeting. The operator of the recorder shall remain seated in the area set aside for the general public or stand in the rear or to the side of the general public seating area so as to not interfere in any way with the activities of the Select Board or the ability of the general public to observe the Board. III. A. B. C. D. E. F. G. H. PUBLIC COMMENT Residents and taxpayers of Lanesborough shall have the right to speak in the meetings during the Public Comment portion of the agenda. In order to conduct meetings in an orderly and productive manner the following rules and regulations shall govern such speakers: Comment from residents/taxpayers shall be received only after the speaker is recognized by the Chairman. The speaker shall announce his or her name and address prior to addressing the Select Board. The Chairman may rule out-of-order scandalous, impertinent, irrelevant, and redundant comments, or comments that attempt to disrupt or needlessly protract the proceedings of the meeting. The Chairman may request any individual to leave the meeting and may contact security to that end when that individual does not observe reasonable decorum. Further, the Chairman may request the assistance of law enforcement officers to remove a disorderly person when his/her conduct interferes with the orderly progress of the meeting. The Chairman may call a recess or adjournment to another time when the lack of public decorum interferes with the orderly conduct of the meeting. The Chairman may allocate available time among individuals wishing to comment. Time allocated for the public comment period at each meeting shall not exceed thirty (30) minutes and limited to citizens of Lanesborough unless prior approval is granted by the Lanesborough Select Board. Each speaker will be allotted three (3) minutes to present his or her topic. Said time limitations may be altered or waived at the Chairman’s direction. At the discretion of the Chairman conducting the meeting, a group of citizens registered to address the Select Board on the same issue may be required to designate a spokesperson.

text: Town of Lenox Conservation Commission Meeting Agenda Thursday October 1st, 2026 7:00 PM Town Hall, 6 Walker Street Land Use Room Request for Certificate of Compliance ~ Lime Kiln Road, DEP #198-0214 2004 Notice of Intent — continued discussion of 525 Pittsfield Road, former Lenox Inn, DEP #198-0357. Applicant proposes to redevelop the existing motel into a gas station and convenience store with related site work and new utility connections, as well as restoration and expansion of an existing drain outfall. Work will be performed within the 100 foot buffer zone of a Bordering Vegetated Wetland. Notice of intent — 48 Sargent Brook Road. Applicant proposes to construct an addition with a crawl space foundation to the existing dwelling and to replace and slightly extend existing deck structures, The proposed project, including existing structures, lies with the 100’ buffer zone of Laurel Lake. Additionally, septic system upgrades are proposed in an area within the Riverfront to Sargent Brook and a new dock will be installed, pending a Chapter 91 permit. Notice of Intent ~ 0 East Street, Hallowell Meadows. The applicant proposes to construct a three-car parking area adjacent to East Street with trail information kiosk, as well as a walking trail loop with bog bridge. An existing collapsed footbridge will be removed. The proposed project areas fall within a Bordering Vegetated Wetland, crosses four intermittent stream reaches and follows along a perennial stream in certain areas. Discussion of mowing at Edith Wharton Park Approval of Minutes- September 16th, 2026

text: COMMONWEALTH OF MASSACHUSETTS WILLIAM FRANCIS GALVIN SECRETARY OF THE COMMONWEALTH WARRANT FOR LOCAL ELECTION SS. Additional Information Board Action Motion Second In favor Opposed Disposition Littleton Code Enforcement: 40U Overview Prepared and Presented by Peter A. Brown, Esq. and Joseph P. Ertl, Esq. Overview/Preview I. Expansion of Existing and Successful Code Enforcement II. Recommended System 2 Describing the Problem 1. Abandoned Properties/Neglected by Owners 2. Bank Owned/Controlled Properties 3. No Accessible Equity to Owner 4. Tickets against the Person Don’t Work 5. Tickets against the Bank Don’t Work SOLUTION :Getting to the equity is the key to compliance 3 Describing the Problem Broader Applications of Chapter 40U 1. Stalled repairs or demolition after fire 1. Properties with history of criminal activities and numerous code violations (trash, unregistered vehicles, illegal scrapping, arson, theft, drug activity) 2. Highrise buildings with issues like non-operational elevators for elderly and disabled residents 3. Commercial properties with zoning and sanitary code violations (depending on the circumstances) 4 Goal of the Program • Provide a Legal Process designed to maximize the ability for the Town to address properties out of code compliance • Expanding the existing code enforcement framework to provide necessary tools to handle the most problematic properties • Ensure appeal-proof processes on inspections, corrective requirements, fines, liens, and administrative warrants • Lay out road to compliance • Owner agrees to do all of the work contained in the Order to Correct (OTC) and pull necessary permits • Work is monitored and the case is closed when the work is completed and it’s determined property is fully code compliant • Operate at a cost-neutral and potentially revenue generating level • Ensure success through cross-departmental belief and trust in the system 5 Recommended System 1. Operate under Chapter 40U 2. Transition ticketing under the State Sanitary Code for the most troubled properties 3.Current systems remain in effect • 40U is a complimentary tool when needed 6 Advantages of Chapter 40U 1. Ticketing against the property vs. the person • M.G.L. c. 40U – Up to $500.00 2. Minimal Court involvement • • Fines imposed through an administrative hearing process Liens secured as a matter of law 3. More control • Everything is brought in-house 7 Authority under the State Sanitary Code • State Sanitary Code has the most potent authority (105 CMR 410.000 et seq.) • Foundation for the strongest Orders to Correct • Easiest path to get to the owner’s Tax Bill • Backs up plan of action (i.e., Administrative Search Warrants, Receiverships, etc.) • Vast majority of Building, Electrical, Plumbing, Fire Code violations are also violations of the State Sanitary Code 8 9 Terminology for Ticketing Status (MGL. c. 40U) CODE TICKET 40U LIEN TAX BILL TAX TITLE Within 51 days of issuance or pending MHO appeal Gone through 40U flowchart without payment/not fully appealed; Lien against RE – just like an overdue water/sewer bill Unpaid lien added to the actual bill(s) Property has a recorded tax taking 10 Most Problematic Properties/Code Enforcement Task Force • Special process for the Worst of the Worst Properties • • • • • Title Check (determine legal owners and interested parties) Collecting Evidence via thorough inspections ASW Detailed Orders to Correct Follow Ups with appropriate Code Enforcement and monitoring until full compliance (could include: ticketing, condemnations, demolition orders if/when applicable) Personnel and Resources • Code Enforcement Team: Building, Health, Fire, and Legal • Tickets: Issuance, Delivery, Letters • Ticket Tracking: Keeping Spreadsheet, 30 day Letters, Monitoring Appeals • Hearings: MHO, Scheduling, Notice, Informing Owner of Decisions • MLC Process and Communication System: Coordination with the Finance Dept. • Funds for Emergency Clean Ups and Property Remediation to protect the neighborhood 12 Where to find us: Website: www.brownlegalllc.com Instagram: @brownlgalpllc X: @brownlegalpllc Facebook: Brown Legal PLLC LinkedIn: Brown Legal PLLC Email: brown@brownlegalllc.com & ertl@brownlegalllc.com 13 Littleton Select Board AGENDA ACTION REQUEST October 5, 2026 6A Informational Presentation Presentation of Historic Preservation Awards Requested by: Linda Stein, Chair Historical Commission Proposed Motion(s) Discussion dependent. text: Marshfield Zoning Board of Appeals 870 Moraine Street, Marshfield, MA 02050 TUESDAY, October 27, 2026 at 6:30 P.M. NOTICE OF PUBLIC HEARING Pursuant to Chapter 2 of the Acts of 2023 dated March 29, 2023, An Act Relative to Extending Certain COVID 19 Measures Adopted During the State of Emergency regarding suspending certain provisions of the Open Meeting Law, G. L. c. 30A §18, the Town of Marshfield’s Zoning Board of Appeals Meeting will be conducted both in-person and via remote participation. For this meeting, members of the public may attend in-person or may participate remotely, a hybrid form of meeting, also utilizing the ZOOM Meeting Instructions (video and phone in instructions) listed below. The public may also view the meeting by viewing the Town of Marshfield’s government access channels: Verizon (Chanel 35) and Comcast (Channel 15). Every effort will be made to ensure that members and the public can adequately access the proceedings to the best of our technical abilities; and, despite our best efforts, this meeting may be viewed as a video recording on Marshfield Community Television website (marshfieldtv.org) and a transcript or other comprehensive record of the meeting will be available as soon as possible after the meeting. Please note that while an option for remote attendance and/or participation is being provided as a courtesy to the public, the meeting/hearing will not be suspended or terminated if technological problems interrupt the virtual broadcast, unless required by law. If participating remotely, you must have microphone or you will not be able to speak. You must have camera if you want to see video. A Public Hearing will be held by the MARSHFIELD ZONING BOARD OF APPEALS on Tuesday, October 27, 2026 at 6:30 P.M. to consider the following: #26-56: Bradford F. Maltby Jr. and Gabrielle F. Barcomb – The Petitioner is seeking a Variance in accordance § 305-10.11 from the height requirements of § 305-6.07 of the Marshfield Municipal Code to allow for the construction of a two-story accessory building that is 29.1’ in height on the nonconforming property located at 333 Elm Street, which is further identified on the Assessors’ Maps as being on parcel H15-03-03 and is located in the R-1 Zoning District. #26-57: Town of Marshfield Airport Commission – The Petitioner is seeking Site Plan Approval in accordance § 305-12.02 of the Marshfield Municipal Code to allow demolition of an existing accessory storage building and replacement with a new, floodproofed accessory storage building in its place on the property located at 93 Old Colony Lane, which is further identified on the Assessors’ Maps as being on parcel K09-03-03A and is located in the A Zoning District. The Petitioners and all interested parties are advised to check the Town website and/or Zoning Board of Appeals homepage for additional information and details. Brian Murphy, Chair Stephen Lynch Grover Hensley, Jr., Vice Chair Eric Murphy Mary Ann Brogan Larry Keane, Clerk Mack Brothers

text: TOWN OF MARSHFIELD SPECIAL TOWN MEETING MONDAY, OCTOBER 19, 2026 at 7:00 P.M. at MARSHFIELD HIGH SCHOOL AUDITORIUM Please bring this report to Town Meeting. Reminder – State Law prohibits SMOKING on school property. MUNICIPAL FINANCE TERMS APPROPRIATION – An authorization by the Town Meeting to make obligations and payments from the treasury for a specific purpose. ASSESSED VALUATION – A valuation set upon real or personal property by the Board of Assessors as a basis for levying taxes. BETTERMENT – A betterment assessment is a charge for the cost of public improvements, which benefit a limited area, against real estate situated in such. BAN – “Bond Anticipatory Note”. Short term borrowing done in advance of long term borrowing via issuance of a BOND. BANs are issued to be able to fund a project while waiting to go to formal bonding. BOND – A loan, typically over a year in maturity. BOND AUTHORIZATION – The amount of money the Town Meeting approves for borrowing for a specific purpose. BOND / BAN PREMIUM – Funds paid to the Town by financial institutions as commissions on the sale of the Town’s BONDS or BANs. These premiums are allowed under the Massachusetts Municipal Act of 2016 under Chapter 44, section 20 to be used to fund similar Capital Projects to the projects funded by the original BOND/BAN. BOND ISSUE – Generally, the sale of a certain number of bonds at one time by a governmental unit. CAPITAL BUDGET – A plan of proposed capital outlays and the means of financing them for the current fiscal period. CAPITAL OUTLAY – An expenditure for the purchase of property or equipment and for the construction or renovation of a facility and infrastructure. CHERRY SHEET – A form showing all state and county charges and reimbursements to the town as certified by the Massachusetts Department of Revenue. DEBT SERVICE – Payment of interest and repayment of principal to holders of the town’s debt instruments. ENTERPRISE FUND – Financing of services where all or most of the costs are paid for by users. ENTERPRISE RETAINED EARNINGS – If during a fiscal year an Enterprise fund produces a surplus, such surplus shall be kept in a separate account called “retained earnings”. The Department of Revenue then certifies that surplus as an available fund which can be used for: 1. operating costs to offset the need to increase user charges, 2. to fund capital improvements, 3. to reimburse General Fund to the extent the General Fund has funded a particular service in prior years, or 4. to fund Enterprise Fund revenue deficits. FISCAL YEAR - A 12-month period, commencing on July 1, to which the annual budget applies. (Abbreviated as "FY".) FREE CASH - The excess of assets over liabilities, minus uncollected taxes of prior years, also referred to as "available cash". The amount is certified annually by the Massachusetts Department of Revenue. Free Cash may be appropriated by vote of a town meeting. GENERAL FUND - The major town owned fund which is created with town receipts and which is charged with expenditures payable from such revenues. GRANT - A contribution of assets by one governmental unit or other organization to another. Typically, these contributions are made to local governments from the state and federal government. Grants are usually made for specific purposes. LEVY LIMIT - The amount of dollars a Town can raise by taxation under Proposition 2 1/2. LINE-ITEM BUDGET - A format of budgeting which organizes costs by type of expenditure. Such as expenses, equipment, and salaries. OVERLAY - The overlay is the amount raised by the Assessors to be used for potential abatement of property taxes. The Overlay Surplus is the portion of each year's overlay account no longer required to cover property tax abatements. PROPERTY TAX LEVY - The amount produced by multiplying the assessed valuation of property by the tax rate. The tax rate is expressed "per thousand dollars" of assessed valuation. RESERVE FUND - Money set aside by Town Meeting to be allocated by the Advisory Board for extraordinary and unforeseen expenditures. REVOLVING FUND (Ch.44, Sec. 53E 1/2) - A Town may annually authorize the use of a revolving fund by accounting for separately the receipts received from a particular service or program and expend from such fund for providing such service or program without appropriation. STABILIZATION FUND - A special account which is invested until used and can only be utilized by town meeting appropriation. Board of Public Works, Select Board, Open Space and Community Preservation Committees Recommendations: At Town Meeting. 4 Article 4 Explanation: The primary purpose of this acquisition is to protect the Furnace Brook well site on Main Street by preventing redevelopment of the property. The property is located within the Zone I (400-foot radius around the well) of the Furnace Brook 3 Drinking Water Well. MassDEP requires public water systems to own or legally control their well's Zone I protective radius and restrict land use strictly to water supply operations or non-threatening activities. Due to that restriction, the septic system for this property is located on adjacent Town property 401 feet from the well. Owning the property will allow the Town to fully control the Zone I for this well that is a critical source of drinking water providing back up water supply during periods of low water flow. Enhanced protection of this well site is part of the DPW’s long-term strategy to prioritize wells in vulnerable locations. This acquisition is an important proactive measure to help prevent contamination from PFAS chemicals and other contaminants and avoid future costs for water treatment. The developed portion of the property is upgradient from a wetland resource area consisting of deep and shallow marsh which could serve as a pathway for contaminants to easily migrate toward the well. The existing house will be removed and the site closed to public access and protected in perpetuity with a Conservation Restriction. ARTICLE 5 Will the Town vote to appropriate the sum of $33,000 in acquisition and restriction costs, and $530,000 in land purchase expense, for a total appropriation of $563,000 from CPC Undesignated reserves to enable the Town to acquire for water resource protection, open space, passive recreation, and/or conservation purposes under Mass. Gen. L. Chapter 44B, the Community Preservation Act, the land with the buildings and improvements thereon known as and numbered 235 Main Street, Marshfield, Massachusetts consisting of two parcels of land, known as and numbered 235 Main Street, Marshfield, Plymouth County, Massachusetts and more particularly described in a deeds recorded with Plymouth Registry of Deeds at Book 60010, Page 123 and Book 60257, Page 339 and also shown on the Town of Marshfield Assessors’ Maps as Parcels G09-01-12 and G09-01-18 containing 3.92 acres of land, more or less; said land to be held under the care and custody of the Board of Public Works and/or the Marshfield Conservation Commission; and further, to authorize the Board of Public Works, Conservation Commission and/or the Select Board to submit on behalf of the town any and all applications deemed necessary for grants and/or reimbursements from the Commonwealth of Massachusetts, or the United States, under the Self-Help Act (Mass. Gen. L. Chapter 132A § 11) and/or any other state or federal programs including those in aid of conservation land and/or drinking water protection; and/or any others in any way connected with the scope of this Article; and further, that the Select Board be directed to grant a perpetual open space and/or conservation restriction in said parcel of land meeting the requirements of Mass. Gen. L. Chapter 44B, § 12 and/or Mass. Gen. L. Chapter 184, §§ 31-33, and to enter into all agreements and execute any and all instruments as may be necessary to affect said purchase, said funds to be expended by the Select Board and the Community Preservation Committee; or take any other action thereon. 5 Board of Public Works, Select Board, Open Space and Community Preservation Committees Recommendations: At Town Meeting. Article 5 Explanation: The primary purpose of this acquisition is to protect the Furnace Brook well site on Main Street by preventing redevelopment of the property and the installation of a septic system near the well. The Furnace Brook well is a critical source of drinking water that provides back up water supply during periods of low water flow. Enhanced protection of this well site is part of the DPW’s long-term strategy to prioritize wells in vulnerable locations. Due to the property location, topography, adjacent wetlands associated with the Furnace Brook well and proximity to the Zone 1 water supply area, this acquisition is an important proactive measure to help prevent contamination from PFAS chemicals and other contaminants and avoid future costs for water treatment. The property is located within Zone 11of the Water Resource Protection District and is approximately 527 ft from the well. The developed portion of the property is upgradient from a wetland resource area consisting of deep and shallow marsh which could serve as a pathway for contaminants to easily migrate toward the well. The existing house will be removed and the site closed to public access and protected in perpetuity with a Conservation Restriction. ARTICLE 6 Will the Town vote to appropriate the sum of $58,000 in acquisition and restriction costs, and $1,125,000 in land purchase expense, for a total appropriation of $1,183,000 from CPC Undesignated reserves to enable the Town to acquire for water resource protection, open space, passive recreation, and/or conservation purposes under Mass. Gen. L. Chapter 44B, the Community Preservation Act, and to authorize the Select Board to accept the deed to the town of fee simple interest or less, of a parcel of land known as and numbered off Holly Road, Marshfield, Massachusetts consisting of a certain parcels of vacant land known as land off Holly Road Marshfield, Plymouth County, Massachusetts and more particularly shown on the Town of Marshfield Assessors’ Maps as Parcel H14-04-18A and containing 30.98 acres of land, more or less, and more particularly described in a deed recorded in Plymouth County Registry of Deeds at Book 28705, Page 261-263 standing in the name of Chestnut Hill Estates, LLC; said land to be held under the care and custody of the Board of Public Works and/or the Marshfield Conservation Commission; and further, to authorize the Board of Public Works, Conservation Commission and/or the Select Board to submit on behalf of the town any and all applications deemed necessary for grants and/or reimbursements from the Commonwealth of Massachusetts, or the United States, under the Self-Help Act (Mass. Gen. L. Chapter 132A § 11) and/or any other state or federal programs including those in aid of conservation land and/or drinking water protection; and/or any others in any way connected with the scope of this Article; and further, that the Select Board be directed to grant a perpetual open space and/or conservation 6 restriction in said parcel of land meeting the requirements of Mass. Gen. L. Chapter 44B, § 12 and/or Mass. Gen. L. Chapter 184, §§ 31-33, and to enter into all agreements and execute any and all instruments as may be necessary to affect said purchase, said funds to be expended by the Select Board and the Community Preservation Committee; or take any other action thereon. Board of Public Works, Select Board, Open Space and Community Preservation Committees Recommendations: At Town Meeting. Article 6 Explanation: The primary purpose of acquiring the 30.98-acre property is to expand the town’s open space inventory, thereby improving the General Land Area Minimum (GLAM) calculation and helping the town meet the threshold needed to avoid mandatory 40B developments in the future. The site contains high-value conservation land, making it a priority for acquisition and permanent protection. The entire property lies within the Zone 11 Water Supply … to effectuate the purposes hereof, or take any other action relative thereto, including removal of the Brant Rock Village Overlay District references and boundaries from our Zoning maps. Lawler, P.C., representing James Dolan and Erin Dolan (“Appellants”), appeals the Building Commissioner’s Zoning Determination pursuant to M.G.L. c. 40A, §§ 7, 8, and 15, which determined that the accessory structure is in violation of the 1985 variance decision. (Continued from September 23, 2026, hearings). NEW HEARINGS 71-B Echo Road: Petitioner, Charlie Schmalz, Owner of Sand & Reef requests a Modification to an existing Special Permit (SP-2015-13), under §174-25 (G) (9) of the Zoning Bylaws to allow for boat storage of up to (14) fourteen boats on property located in an I-1 Zoning District, Map 19, Parcel 3-5, Mashpee, MA (Owner of Record: DECH, LLC). 1 of 2 RECEIVED by Town Clerk’s Office 10/7/2026 9:18 AM Mashpee, MA Agenda Zoning Board of Appeals October 14, 2026 Page 2 22 & 26 Oyster Way: Petitioner, Tanya D. CONTINUED HEARINGS Route 28 and Jobs Fishing Road: Petitioner, On Commons LLC C/O, Blatman, Bobrowski, Haverty & Silverstein, LLC is requesting a Comprehensive Permit under M.G.L. 40B §§20-23 to construct sixty-five (65) rental units, including seventeen (17) affordable units on a 1.86-acre site located at the corner of Job’s Fishing Road and Falmouth Road (Route 28), on property located in a C-1 Zoning District, Map 74, Parcel 20A-3, Mashpee, MA. (508) 865-9110 • EMAIL: TownClerk@millburyma.gov Members: Mary Krumsiek, Chairperson Brian Sora, Vice Chairperson Nicholas Lazzaro, Clerk Brian Tagg Michael Gilchrist By Town Clerk at 12:16 pm, Oct 05, 2026 Board of Selectmen Amended Special Meeting Notice & Agenda Date: 10/8/26 Time: 6:30 PM Location: 127 Elm St, Millbury MA, Selectmen's Room ZOOM Meeting ID & Call in: Meeting ID: 823 3190 3417 One tap mobile +13052241968,,82331903417# +13092053325,,82331903417# "Welcome to the October 8, 2026, meeting of the Board of Selectmen. This meeting is being recorded and streamed by Millbury Public Access Cable Television, available live on public access channels, Charter 191 or Verizon 26. text: TOWN OF MONSON RECEIVED SELECT BOARD OCT OB 2025 300 REGULAR MEETING AGENDA TOWN CLERK, MONSON, MA DATE: Tuesday, October 138, 2026 TIME: 7:00 PM LOCATION: 110 MAIN STREET — Public Meeting Room Call To Order We have assistive listening devices available for anyone who needs them. If you'd like to use one, please let a staff member know at any time during the meeting. M-PACT is recording this meeting. Any person may also record this meeting, after notice to the Select Board Chair. In order to run the meeting more efficiently, the Chair requests that persons who would like to speak on an agenda item, do so during public comment. No questions from the public will be taken during the business portion of the meeting. Public questions should be directed to the Executive Assistant at rmorse@monson-ma.gov and will be handled accordingly. Pledge of Allegiance Public Comment The Select Board shall provide a period not to exceed 15 minutes at the beginning of its semi-monthly meetings. Generally, there will be no discussion of topics raised. The following rules are intended to provide a structured format whereby constituents can provide information about, or comment on, items of select board business only. Only an individual recognized by the chair can speak. Audience members may not interrupt a recognized speaker nor the discussion of the body. The speaker is limited to two minutes for their comments. If they have additional remarks beyond this time limit, they may submit them in writing to the Select Board. Each speaker is allowed to speak only once during the public comment period and cannot yield their time to another speaker. The speaker must exercise conduct in an "orderly and peaceable manner". The Board encourages speakers to avoid repeating themselves, and if multiple speakers wish to talk on the same subject, they are encouraged to choose one spokesperson. The speaker may not approach the select board table, including to provide handouts or other materials. If a speaker or audience member violates any rule herein above, is disturbing or impeding the meeting, or threatens violence or incites imminent lawless conduct, the chair shall direct that such conduct shall immediately cease, and if it does not, the chair has the authority to stop the violator, take away any remaining time to speak, and/or in egregious cases, remove the violator from the meeting. text: TOWN OF MONSON SPECIAL TOWN MEETING WARRANT ln bY a fi W A Mactan ES Sime |) me | eat a MONSON a Os ee SET TS FOUNDED s7e0 A. town we eart INCORPORATED 1775 MONDAY, OCTOBER 26, 2026 7:00 PM GRANITE VALLEY SCHOOL COMMONWEALTH OF MASSACHUSETTS HAMPDEN, ss. TOWN OF MONSON SPECIAL TOWN MEETING WARRANT To any of the Constables of the Town of Monson in said County: GREETINGS: In the name of the Commonwealth of Massachusetts, you are hereby directed to notify and warn all the inhabitants of the Town of Monson qualified to vote in Elections and Town Affairs to meet at Granite Valley School on Thompson Street on Monday, October 26, 2026, at 7:00 p.m. to act upon the following articles: CONSENT AGENDA Warrant articles on the Consent Agenda are exceptions to the general process of Town Meeting. The Select Board, Moderator, and Finance Committee identify, for Town Meeting consideration, those articles that they believe should generate no controversy and can be properly voted without debate. These articles are put on the Consent Agenda to allow motions under these articles to be acted upon as one unit and to be passed without debate. At the call of the Consent Agenda, the Moderator will read out the numbers of the articles, one by one. If one or more voters object to any article being included in the Consent Agenda, they say “hold” in a loud voice when the number is called. The article will be removed automatically from the Consent Agenda and restored to its original place in the Warrant, to be debated and voted in the usual manner. After the calling of the individual items in the Consent Agenda, the Moderator will ask for a motion that the voters pass all items remaining AS A UNIT in one vote. Use of the Consent Agenda process makes the Town Meeting more efficient by speeding up the handling of non-controversial items. Please review the list of articles and motions proposed for each Consent Item which follows: MOTION: Moved that the Town take Articles 1, 2, 3, 4, 5, 6, and 7 that they be “Passed by Consent” in accordance with the recommendations as printed in the warrant. Explanation: The sum of $30,412.61 is being requested to cover FY26 prior year bill. Recommendation: Finance Committee Recommends, and I Move the Town Vote to transfer $30,412.61 from the Sewer Enterprise Retained Earnings to the prior year bills account. ARTICLE 5: (consent agenda) Submitted By: Water & Sewer Department Required Vote: Majority To see if the Town will vote to transfer and appropriate from the Sewer Enterprise Retained Earnings a sum of money to the Inflow & Infiltration (I&I) and Repair Project Account, or take any other action relative thereto. Explanation: The sum of $60,000.00 is being requested for Year 2 1&1 Remediation Work and Engineering Services. Recommendation: Finance Committee Recommends, and I Move the Town Vote to transfer $60,000 from the Sewer Enterprise Retained Earnings as printed in the warrant. ARTICLE 6: (consent agenda) Submitted By: Water & Sewer Department Required Vote: Majority To see if the Town will vote to transfer and appropriate from the Sewer Enterprise Retained Earnings a sum of money for costs and expenses related to Hospital Road Sewer Station Wastewater Pump equipment repairs at the or take any other action relative thereto. Explanation: The sum of $9,130.00 is being requested to cover expenses for necessary pump maintenance. Recommendation: Finance Committee Recommends, and I Move the Town Vote to transfer $9,130 from the Sewer Enterprise Retained Earnings as printed in the warrant. ARTICLE 7: (consent agenda) Submitted By: Water & Sewer Department Required Vote: Majority To see if the Town will vote to transfer and appropriate from the Water and Sewer Enterprise Retained Earnings a sum of money for costs and expenses related to Desktop Computer Replacement or take any other action relative thereto. Explanation: The sum of $3,500 is being requested to replace the Superintendents Desktop Computer. Recommendation: Finance Committee Recommends, and I Move the Town Vote to transfer $1,750 from the Sewer Enterprise Retained Earnings and $1,750 from the Water Enterprise Retained Earnings as printed in the warrant. ARTICLE 8: Submitted by: Community Preservation Committee Required Vote: Majority To see if the Town will vote to appropriate the sum of $42,800.00 from the Budgeted Reserves Account of the Community Preservation Program for the restoration and preservation of the Jacob Thompson House roof. Funds will be expended under the direction of the Community Preservation Committee or take any other action thereto. Explanation: The roof of the Jacob Thompson House located at 7 Main Street is leaking and in need of repair. The House is owned by the Monson Historical Society and is on the National Register of Historic Places. The MHS is requesting funds to remove the old asphalt shingles and repair and replace with cedar shingles as would be appropriate for a house built in 1776. Recommendation: Finance Committee Recommends, and I Move the Town Vote as printed in the warrant. ARTICLE 9: Submitted by: School Committee Required Vote: Majority To see if the Town will vote to transfer $88,320.84 from Free Cash to the Special Education Reserve Fund or take any other action relative thereto. Explanation: This article is to transfer the FY26 Medicaid reimbursement funds to the Special Education Reserve Fund to use for unanticipated, extraordinary or volatile special education costs. Recommendation: Finance Committee Recommends, and I Move the Town Vote to transfer $88,320.84 from Free Cash to the Special Education Reserve Fund. ARTICLE 10: Submitted by: Police Chief Required Vote: Majority To see if the Town will vote to transfer from Free Cash a sum of money, to the police department account to purchase tasers or take any other action relative thereto. Explanation: The department’s current Tasers are outdated, unsupported by available software, and present a safety concern. Axon provided quotes for several packages. Based on the department’s needs, the recommended mid-tier package would cost $14,800 annually for five years.

and WHEREAS, in the United States, on average, nearly twenty people per minute are physically abused by an intimate partner, amounting to more than ten million women and men each year, and one in four women and one in nine men experience severe intimate partner physical violence in their lifetime; and WHEREAS, domestic violence has devastating and lasting consequences, including physical injury, emotional trauma, and economic hardship, and it is a leading cause of injury and homelessness among women and children; and WHEREAS, children who witness domestic violence in their homes are profoundly affected, and breaking the cycle of abuse requires the sustained and collective commitment of our entire community; and WHEREAS, the Town of Montague is committed to fostering a community where every resident can live free from fear, intimidation, and abuse, and where survivors are met with compassion, safety, and support; and WHEREAS, local and regional organizations, advocates, law enforcement, healthcare providers, schools, and faith communities work tirelessly to provide critical services to survivors of domestic violence and to promote education, prevention, and awareness; and WHEREAS, the month of October is recognized nationally as Domestic Violence Awareness Month, providing an opportunity to honor survivors, remember those whose lives have been lost, and renew our shared commitment to ending domestic violence in all its forms; NOW, THEREFORE, BE IT RESOLVED that the Selectboard of the Town of Montague does hereby proclaim the month of October 2026 as DOMESTIC VIOLENCE AWARENESS MONTH in the Town of Montague; and The Town of Montague is an equal opportunity provider and employer TOWN OF MONTAGUE MASSACHUSETTS Selectboard Office One Avenue A Turners Falls, MA 01376 413-863-3200 Ext. 108 & 107 BE IT FURTHER RESOLVED that the Selectboard calls upon all residents, businesses, institutions, and organizations of Montague to recognize the impact of domestic violence, to support survivors and the dedicated individuals and agencies who serve them, and to actively work toward a community free from violence and abuse for all. PROCLAIMED this fifth day of October, 2026. Montague Selectboard ___ Richard Kuklewicz Chair ___ Marina Goldman ___ Nate Card The Town of Montague is an equal opportunity provider and employer 6A TOWN OF MONTAGUE DEPUTY POLICE CHIEF CONTRACT Agreement made this 5th day of October, 2026, by and between the TOWN OF MONTAGUE (hereinafter “Town), by and through its Selectboard, and Joshua Hoffman (hereinafter “Deputy Chief”). WHEREAS, The Town is desirous of securing the services of Joshua Hoffman in the administration of the Police Department; and WHEREAS, Joshua Hoffman is willing to perform the duties of the position of Deputy Chief of Police and hereby accepts the appointment to the position of Deputy Chief of Police WHEREAS, the parties wish to negotiate a contract outlining the Deputy Chief’s salary and other employment benefits. NOW, THEREFORE, the Town and Joshua Hoffman hereby agree to the following terms and conditions: 1. DUTIES: The Deputy Chief of Police shall perform the duties as set forth in state law, Town Bylaws, and the applicable job description, a copy of which is attached hereto and incorporated herein by reference. 2. HOURS OF WORK: A. In the exercise of his duties, the Deputy Chief will be expected to be present during normal business hours, with a normal work week of 40 hours, but shall generally be on call twenty-four hours a day except during absences authorized by the Town. The Deputy Chief may adjust his schedule within reasonable limits at his discretion and with approval of the Chief. “Flex” time is allowed and shall be consistent with the policies established by the Town. Said time off shall be taken at times that the Deputy Chief reasonably determines will not adversely impact Department operations. The Deputy Chief shall be considered an exempt employee under the federal Fair Labor Standards Page 1 of 15 Act (FLSA). B. Any planned time off to the extent possible shall be reported to the Chief at least 5 working days before requested time off. The Deputy Chief will coordinate time off with the Chief so coverage is in place and to the extent possible avoid overlapping time off. 3. INSURANCE: A. Indemnification A. To the extent permitted by G.L. c. 258, the Town shall defend, save harmless and indemnify the Deputy Chief against any tort, professional liability claim or demand or other civil or criminal legal action, whether groundless or otherwise, arising out of an alleged act or omission occurring in the performance of the Deputy Chief’s duties. The Town’s indemnification obligations herein shall not extend to any violation of a person’s state or federal civil rights if the Deputy Chief is adjudged to have acted in a grossly negligent, willful, or malicious manner, nor shall the indemnification obligations extend to any disciplinary actions or other proceedings by the Town against the Deputy Chief. The Town, during the term of this Agreement, will maintain adequate professional liability insurance for the Employee in connection with his performance of his duties as Deputy Chief. (This provision shall survive any termination of this agreement concerning acts or omissions while serving as the Deputy Chief.) B. Disability The Deputy Chief shall be entitled to the same sick leave and disability benefits as are available to the other police officers of the Town. C. Miscellaneous The Deputy Chief shall be eligible for all health and life insurance benefits for Page 2 of 15 which other non-bargaining unit, general government employees are eligible. The Town agrees to contribute towards the cost of such insurance premiums an amount or percentage equal to that provided to non-union management of the Town. D. Injured On-Duty As a sworn police officer, the Deputy Chief shall be entitled to injured-on-duty benefits as provided in Chapter 41, Section 111F of the Massachusetts General Laws. 4. AUTOMOBILE: A. The Town shall provide a vehicle for use by the Deputy Chief and pay for all attendant operating and maintenance expenses and insurance. Said vehicle is to be used by the Deputy Chief in connection with the performance of his duties as Chief and he may utilize said vehicle while acting within the scope of his employment with the Town. The Deputy Chief agrees to maintain a valid Class D Massachusetts Driver’s License during the term of this agreement. In recognition of the fact that the Deputy Chief is on-call 24 hours per day, incidental personal use shall be limited to locations within fifty (50) miles of the Town's borders and shall not occur under circumstances that would materially interfere with the Deputy Chief's ability to respond to an emergency or Department need while on call. Incidental personal use may include but not be limited to routine local activities such as grocery shopping, medical appointments, fitness activities, and similar personal errands, provided that such use does not interfere with the Deputy Chief’s ability to respond when required. Family members ordinarily may not be transported in Town vehicles unless they are on official business or otherwise authorized by the Chief. Such personal use shall not be considered to be regular compensation for purposes of retirement pursuant to PERAC regulations. B. In the event the Deputy Chief’s Town- issued vehicle is non-operational, the Town agrees to pay for mileage if the Deputy Chief uses his privately-owned vehicle for official business in accordance with the IRS reimbursement rates. Page 3 of 15 6. PROFESSIONAL DEVELOPMENT: The Deputy Police Chief shall be given opportunities to develop his skills and abilities; accordingly, The Deputy Police Chief shall be allowed to annual in-service training, courses, seminars, and meetings relative to public safety which are approved in the advance by the Chief of Police, this shall include the attending the FBI National Academy. If the Police Chief requires the Deputy Police Chief to attend any course, seminar or meeting, the Department shall pay for the cost of such programs, and for the travel and subsistence expenses incurred by the Deputy Police Chief in attending such programs. Costs for professional memberships, conferences, meetings, and training shall not exceed $5,000 per fiscal year. 7. DEATH DURING TERM OF EMPLOYMENT: If the Deputy Chief dies during the term of his employment, the Town shall pay to the Chiefs estate all the compensation which would otherwise be payable to the Deputy Chief up to the date of the Deputy Chiefs death, including, but not limited to, payment for any unused vacation, personal or other leave days as provided generally to police officers of the Town. 8. COMPENSATION: A. Commencing on October 11, 2026, the Deputy Chief shall be paid a salary of $ 103,001.60, in accordance with Step 8 of Grade C (FY27) of the Town Classification Plan, subject to applicable state and federal withholdings and deductions, and shall be entitled to step increases on July 1, 2027, July 1, 2028, at which point he will have stepped out at Grade C Step 10. In the event that Grade C of the Classification Plan is amended during the term of this contract following a Wage and Classification Study or similar initiative, the Deputy Chief’s base rate shall be amended to reflect the revised figure that is associated with the new Grade C, without a reduction in pay. B. The Deputy Chief shall receive the same benefits as those currently received by all other non-union, management personnel, including, bereavement days, health and life Page 4 of 15 insurance. However, the Deputy Chief shall be entitled to sick leave and longevity benefits as per the NEPBA Sergeants’ contract. and receive work-appropriate clothing, uniform, and cleaning allowances equivalent to the allowances received by other police officers per the NEPBA contract. C. The Deputy Chief will receive a cost-of-living adjustment (COLA) and step adjustment on July 1, 2027. Said COLAs will be equivalent to the COLAs awarded to members of the NAGE bargaining unit for those fiscal years, but shall not exceed a maximum of 2.5% in either year. If a COLA is awarded to NAGE members for the fiscal year beginning July 1, 2028 and July 1, 2029 the Deputy Chief shall be entitled to the same award. D. Employee shall carry forward any accrued sick leave, comp time, personal, and vacation time from his tenure as Sergeant. For the purpose of vacation time, the Town will grant twenty-five (25) days of vacation per year to be granted in accordance with the NAGE contract. The town will grant four (4) days of personal time per year. E. The Deputy Chief may buy back up to one week of unused vacation time at his discretion before each anniversary date of this contract (e.g. October 2027, 2028, and 2029). F. The Deputy Chief is allowed personal use of the department-issued cell phone and shall receive the stipend amount offered to other employees of the town. G. If the Deputy Chief obtains a bachelors degree from an accredited criminal justice program during this contract period, he shall be entitled to a 20% educational incentive starting the next fiscal year (July 1) after the degree is awarded. H. Holiday Pay. The Deputy Chief may be assigned by the Chief to work up to six (6) Page 5 of 15 holidays paid at a rate of one and one-half (1 ½) his regular rate of pay. 9. NO REDUCTION OF BENEFITS: The Town agrees that it shall not at any time during the term of this contract reduce the salary, compensation or other benefits of the Deputy Chief, except to the extent that such reduction is also applied to all other department heads of the Town. 10. TERMINATION AND SEVERANCE PAY: A. The Selectboard may discipline or discharge the Employee for just cause following a notice and hearing. B. In the event that Employee is terminated by the Board before the expiration of the aforesaid term of employment and during such time Employee is willing and capable of performing his duties under this agreement, then in that event the Board agrees to give the Employee six (6) months’ notice, and shall upon mutual agreement of the parties, either continue in the employ of the Town, or in the alternative, to receive a cash sum equal to the salary that would have been actually earned during said six-month period. Said salary to include any and all benefits currently being provided to the employee, including health insurance. C. In the event the Town at any time during the term of this agreement reduces the salary, compensation or other financial benefits of the Employee by five (5) percent or more, or in the event the Town refuses following written notice, to comply with any provisions benefitting Employee herein, or Employee resigns following a request by the Board that he resign, then in that event, Employee may at his option, be deemed "terminated" at the date of such reduction, or such refusal to comply, or such request, within the meaning and context of the herein severance pay provision. D. In the event Employee voluntarily resigns his position with the Town before expiration of the aforesaid term of his employment, the Employee shall give the Board thirty (30) days written notice in advance, unless the parties otherwise agree. In the event of a voluntary resignation of Employee, such benefits as are enumerated in Section 11, paragraph A and B hereinabove, shall not be awarded. Page 6 of 15 E. Termination of the Deputy Chief’s employment shall result in the termination of this contract. 11. MODIFICATION: No change or modification of this contract shall be valid unless it shall be in writing and signed by both of the parties. 12. LAW GOVERNING: This contract shall be construed and governed by the Laws of the Commonwealth of Massachusetts. 13. SEVERABILITY OF PROVISIONS: If any clause or provision of this contract shall be determined to be illegal by a court of competent jurisdiction, the remainder of this contract shall not be affected thereby. 14. LENGTH OF CONTRACT: A. The term of this contract shall be for a period commencing on October 11, 2026 and ending October 10, 2029, unless terminated prior thereto in accordance with Section 11 of this Contract. However, this contract may be extended as provided by its terms. B.

AGENDA Please list below the topics the chair reasonably anticipates will be discussed at the meeting I. CALL TO ORDER II. ANNUAL STRATEGIC PLAN RETREAT III. ADJOURNMENT 1 MEMO To: Select Board Members C. Elizabeth Gibson, Town Manager From: Michelle Ferguson, Raftelis Date: September 28, 2026 Re: Strategic Planning Retreat Preparation I look forward to being with you on October 6th. The purpose of this memo is to help you prepare for the session and share the agenda. Logistics Location: Time: Meeting Trailer, 131 Pleasant Street Tuesday, October 6 from 8:30 AM-1:00 PM Retreat Goals • • Review and update the Town’s Strategic Plan Initiatives Continue the productive working relationship among the Select Board and with Town Administration Norms • • • • Listen with respect o Let others finish before you start talking o Be attentive to the speaker o Disagree agreeably Strive for consensus o Look for opportunities to agree o Remember the power of “if” and “and” Be: o BOLD o Positive and realistic o Candid and honest o Patient and self-aware o Engaged and fully present Have fun! www.raftelis.com Town of Nantucket / October 2026 Strategic Planning Retreat Agenda 1 Agenda Setting the Stage • • • • Welcome and introductions Norms and expectations for the retreat Agenda review Summary of recent retreats and expectations for 2026 (handout) Strategic Plan Update Town staff will provide an update of each Focus Area’s Goals and Initiatives, and the Board will engage in conversation to reaffirm the goal about the priority initiatives in each area. (handout) • • • • Housing (Housing Department Director Kristie Ferrantella) Transportation (Public Works Department Director Drew Patnode) Environmental Leadership (Natural Resources Department Director Jeff Carlson) Efficient & Effective Town Operations (Deputy Town Manager Rick Sears) Special Discussion Topics • • • • Downtown Activities The group will discuss activity in the downtown area, specifically enforcement and the impact of private businesses on public spaces. Municipal Space Needs Staff will present results from a recent municipal space needs retreat in lieu of a new, central municipal facility. Traffic and Parking Traffic and parking continue to be hot issues on the island, with growing demand to address both, specifically in the downtown and mid-island areas. Override In FY26, there were over 70 override questions in approximately 50 Massachusetts communities. With costs of doing business continuing to rise, especially on an island, and the demands for services growing, it’s prudent to discuss the possibility of an override in the future, or measures to be taken to prevent one. Select Board Updates The Select Board will review the current Focus Areas, Goals and Initiatives, and make updates to the Plan. Next Steps & Closing As the session comes to a close, participants will be asked to share closing thoughts about the work done during the retreat.

Purpose: This Policy is adopted to facilitate orderly and efficient public comment periods at meetings of Town public bodies. It will protect the ability of the residents of Nantucket, and other persons, to provide feedback or information to pertinent public bodies regarding matters of public interest, Town initiatives, operations, services, and programs. To allow speakers a fair opportunity to address a public body, and to ensure the public body may accomplish its stated business in an efficient manner, these guidelines seek to ensure compliance with the Open Meeting Law and meet other legal and constitutional obligations. Meetings of public bodies in the Town of Nantucket should be places to engage in orderly and peaceable discourse. B. Authority: Principles of free speech and freedom to petition the government, fundamental rights protected by the United States and Massachusetts Constitutions, prohibit public bodies from preventing all speech that may be upsetting or offensive. As such, this Policy establishes reasonable time, place, and manner restrictions sufficient to facilitate orderly and peaceable public comment periods at meetings of elected and appointed public bodies of the Town. C. Legal Standards: Meetings of public bodies are subject to the requirements of the Open Meeting Law, G.L. c. 30A, §§ 18-25. The Open Meeting Law empowers the chair of a public body to preside at and regulate the proceedings of meetings. Pursuant to G.L c. 30A, § 20(g), no person shall address a meeting of a public body without permission of the chair, and all persons shall, at the request of the chair, be silent. Any person wishing to speak at an open meeting must first be recognized by the chair. All questions raised and all comments made by a duly-recognized speaker must be directed to the chair of the public body alone, not to individual members of the public body, staff, or the public. The chair is authorized to maintain order, and, although a rare occurrence, has authority, after appropriate warnings are ignored, to take action up to and including removal of a person who is disrupting a meeting. D. Application: To secure the rights of the public to participate in public comment periods in the Town of Nantucket in a manner consistent with law, and, to thereby protect the Town and members of elected and appointed bodies from civil rights claims, this policy shall apply to all public bodies in the Town of Nantucket. E. Procedures: 1. All agendas of multiple-member bodies in the Town of Nantucket shall include a period for Public Comment, subject to the limitations set forth in paragraph 3. Where to place Public Comment on the agenda is at the discretion of the chair. If public comment is invited during a separate agenda item, this Policy shall govern. 2. While statements made during a Public Comment period are not required to address an agenda item for that particular meeting, such comments must relate to a matter within the public body’s jurisdiction. Public comments on matters outside the public body’s jurisdiction may be ruled out of order by the chair. To avoid due process issues, a person seeking to provide comments on a matter appearing on the same agenda will be asked to defer until the specific agenda item is reached. 3. Each speaker will be allowed to speak once for up to 3 minutes. The chair will curtail verbal comments exceeding the allotted time. 4. A recognized speaker may not cede or assign their time to another unless such an assignment is required as reasonable accommodation for such person because of a disability. All speakers who may need an accommodation are strongly encouraged to contact Town staff or the chair of the public body at least 48 hours prior to the meeting. That said, to facilitate an efficient public comment period, groups that have multiple speakers with the same viewpoint may consider consolidating their comments or designating one person to speak on their individual behalf’s. F. Disruptive Conduct/Unprotected Speech: Disruptive conduct and engaging in other unprotected speech, including but not limited to the following, may be grounds for the chair of a public body to curtail speech and take other action as appropriate: 1. Speaking without being recognized; 2. Continuing to speak after the chair has curtailed additional verbal comment; 3. Interrupting a recognized speaker; 4. Speaking about matters not within the jurisdiction of the public body; 5. Engaging in conversations while another person is speaking; 6. Making true threats of violence directed toward a particular individual; and 7. Making comments inciting imminent lawlessness. G. Public Body Response: 1. A public comment period is a listening session, and the public body is there to listen. The public body, in fact, should not respond to matters raised at the meeting unless they are on the agenda for the same meeting. 2. Matters raised during public comment periods are not required to, and are unlikely to, be addressed or resolved by the public body at the same meeting. Such matters may be appropriately deferred to a noticed-agenda item at a future meeting due to Open Meeting Law considerations. 3. At the sole discretion of the chair of the public body, matters raised during public comment may or may not appear on a future agenda or be referred to the Town Administrator for appropriate action, if any. 4. A public body cannot demand that persons attending meetings or participating in public comment be civil to one another. Nevertheless, the Town, or the members of the public, and those that appear before them are encouraged to make any/or all residents of the Town feel welcome, including listening to them speak, and acknowledging that speakers may have a different viewpoints. Disclaimer: A Public Comment period is not a time for debate or response to comments by the public body. Comments made during the Public Comment period do not reflect the views or the positions of the public body. Because of constitutional free speech principles, the public body does not have the authority to prevent all speech that may be upsetting and/or offensive during the public portion of the meeting. H. Enforcement: Concerns about Public Comment Periods may be brought to the attention of the Town Manager, who will discuss the concerns with the chair of the public body, and take appropriate action. Failure to comply with this Policy may be deemed a violation of the Town’s Code of Conduct, and grounds for the removal of an appointed official. Connection to sewers installed with municipal funding.
