text: TOWN OF HINGHAM WARRANT for the SPECIAL TOWN MEETING Thursday, October 29, 2026 at 7:00 P.M. Hingham High School 17 Union Street, Hingham, MA Please bring this report to the meeting for use in the proceedings TABLE OF CONTENTS Page 2 Town Meeting Procedures 20 Municipal Finance Terms 21 Talent Bank Application Special Town Election 4 Page Call of Town Meeting and Town Election Article Special Town Meeting Articles 5 1 South Elementary School Roof 10 2 Plymouth River Elementary School Roof 15 3 High School Roof and HVAC Design 1 MODERATOR'S MESSAGE ON TOWN MEETING PROCEDURES Welcome to the 2026 Hingham Special Town Meeting. In our commitment to open town meeting, Hingham remains true to a wonderful tradition – a tradition that allows each registered voter to play a pivotal role in the governance of the town and to do so with “voice and vote”. Town meeting is not only a gathering of citizens to consider matters of common concern; it is the legislative body of the town. As such, the meeting must be conducted in a fair and open manner and in accordance with the Town Bylaws, as well as traditions that we have followed in Hingham town meetings for many years. Several matters of procedure are summarized below.  An article in the warrant states a question for the town meeting to answer. A motion is a proposed answer to the question and must be within the scope of the article. An article (once published in the warrant) may not be amended, but a motion may be amended by vote of the meeting. All motions must be seconded.  If the Advisory Committee is recommending an affirmative motion under an article, its motion will be received as the main motion under the article. A voter may propose to amend this motion, either to change it in part or to substitute a whole new motion (sometimes called a "substitute motion"). In any such case, the proposed amendment will be taken up and voted on first and then the main motion, as it may have been amended, will be acted upon.  If the Advisory Committee is recommending no action under an article and a voter offers an affirmative motion, the voter's motion will be received as the main motion under the article. Such a motion is likewise subject to amendment.  All motions and proposed amendments involving the expenditure of money must be in writing. So must all other motions and proposed amendments unless they are so brief and simple as to be easily understood when stated orally (e.g., motion for the previous question, motion to adjourn). Voters are welcome to seek the assistance of counsel for the Town in preparing motions or proposed amendments.  Limits on speaking: No one may speak on any subject for more than six (6) minutes for the first time or for more than three (3) minutes for the second time. No one may speak more than twice on any question unless all others who have not spoken on the question shall have spoken if they desire to do so and unless leave of the meeting is first obtained. A person may speak more than twice, but only to make a brief correction of an error in or misunderstanding of his or her previous statement, including brief answers to questions from the floor (addressed through the Moderator).  In addressing the meeting, a speaker shall confine his or her remarks to the matter before the meeting.  Persons who are not registered voters of the Town may be admitted to the meeting as guests by the Moderator. A guest of the meeting may be granted permission to address the meeting by majority vote.  The purpose of the motion for the previous question is to end discussion and have an immediate vote on the pending question. The motion is not debatable and requires a majority vote for adoption. The Moderator will decline to accept a motion for the previous question if 2 other voters are seeking recognition and if both sides have not had a fair opportunity to be heard. The Moderator will accept the motion for the previous question if it appears that both sides have been heard and the discussion is becoming repetitious.  Voting procedures: All votes are taken in the first instance by voice vote. If the Moderator is in doubt as to the results or if seven (7) voters rise and express doubt as to the result declared by the Moderator, a standing vote is taken, except that a ballot vote is taken (instead of a standing vote) if either the Advisory Committee or fifty (50) voters promptly call for a ballot vote. As a ballot vote takes considerable time, our practice has been not to request a ballot vote in the absence of compelling reasons.  At a Special Town Meeting, no money may be appropriated for any purpose if the Advisory Committee recommends against the appropriation, except by a two-thirds vote of the meeting.  No vote may be reconsidered except after a two-thirds vote on a motion to reconsider such vote. A vote may not be reconsidered a second time or after a motion to reconsider it has failed to pass.  A vote adopted at one session of the town meeting may not be reconsidered at a later (adjourned) session of the meeting unless the mover has given notice of the mover’s intention to make such a motion either at the session of the meeting at which the vote was passed or by written notice to the Town Clerk not less than 12 hours before the hour to which adjournment has been voted and not more than 48 hours after the hour of adjournment of such session. Any motion for reconsideration pursuant to such notice of intention will be taken up at the beginning of the adjourned session.  Articles in the warrant are to be acted upon in their order unless the meeting otherwise determines by majority vote.  A motion to adjourn the meeting to a later time is a privileged motion and is decided by majority vote without debate. When the warrant is completed, a motion to dissolve the meeting is in order.  The number of voters constituting a quorum in order to convene the first session of a Regular or Special Town Meeting is 300. The number of voters necessary to convene the second or any subsequent session of a Regular or Special Town Meeting is 200. Once convened, the quorum to transaction business at any Regular or Special Town Meeting is 200; provided, however, that a number of less than 200 may from time to time adjourn the same. Once a quorum is determined at the start of the meeting (or adjourned session), the presence of a quorum is presumed to continue unless a point of no quorum is raised and a count of the meeting shows that a quorum is not present. In that event, the meeting may be adjourned to a later date.  If you wish to speak, please rise and seek the attention of the Moderator or the Assistant Moderator. When recognized by the Moderator, you should come to a microphone. Please state your name and address at the outset each time you speak. Michael J. Puzo Moderator October 2026 3 COMMONWEALTH OF MASSACHUSETTS Plymouth, ss. To the Constables of the Town of Hingham in the County of Plymouth, Greetings: In the name of the Commonwealth of Massachusetts, you are hereby directed to notify and warn the inhabitants of the Town of Hingham qualified to vote in Town affairs to meet at the Hingham High School, 17 Union Street, in said Hingham, on Thursday October 29, 2026 at 7:00 pm, then and there to act on the Warrant Articles listed below. You are hereby also directed to notify and warn the inhabitants of the Town of Hingham qualified to vote in Town affairs to meet at three designated polling places in said Town of Hingham according to their precinct, to wit: Precinct 1, 2, 3, and 4: High School, 17 Union Street; Precincts 5, 6, and 7: Middle School, 1103 Main Street; and Precinct 7A: Willard Square at Linden Ponds on Tuesday, November 3, 2026 from 7:00 am until 8:00 pm, then and there to give their votes on the official ballot for: to give their votes “Yes” or “No” on the following Town ballot questions: • Plymouth River Elementary School: Shall the Town of Hingham be allowed to exempt from the provisions of proposition two and one-half, so-called, the amounts required to pay for the bond issued in order to pay the costs of the roof system replacement, including the payment of all costs incidental or related thereto, at the Plymouth River Elementary School located at 200 High Street, Hingham, MA? • South Elementary School: Shall the Town of Hingham be allowed to exempt from the provisions of proposition two and one-half, so-called, the amounts required to pay for the bond issued in order to pay the costs of the roof system replacement, including the payment of all costs incidental or related thereto, at the South Elementary School located at 831 Main Street, Hingham, MA? Hereof fail not and make due return of this warrant with your doings thereon to the Town Clerk on or before October 1, 2026. Given under our hands at Hingham this twenty-ninth day of September 2026. Elizabeth F. Klein, Chair___ William C. Ramsey ___ Julie M. Strehle___ SELECT BOARD A true copy Attest: By virtue of the within warrant I hereby certify that I have noticed and warned the inhabitants of the Town of Hingham, qualified to vote in Town affairs to meet at the time and place indicated in the above warrant by causing a notice thereof to be published in The Hingham Journal fourteen days at least before the day appointed for said meeting. An attested copy was presented and posted by the Town Clerk in the Town Hall as of this date. ___ Horatio Hemmings Constable of Hingham October 1, 2026 4 ARTICLE 1 SOUTH ELEMENTARY SCHOOL ROOF Will the Town raise and appropriate, borrow or transfer from available funds, a sufficient sum of money to be expended under the direction of the 2025 School Building Committee for the roof system replacement, including the payment of all costs incidental or related thereto (the “Project”), at the South Elementary School located at 831 Main Street, Hingham, MA, which proposed repair Project would materially extend the useful life of the school and preserve an asset that otherwise is capable of supporting the required educational program, and for which the Town may be eligible for a school construction grant from the Massachusetts School Building Authority (“MSBA”). The Town acknowledges that the MSBA’s grant program is a non-entitlement, discretionary program based on need, as determined by the MSBA, and any Project costs the Town incurs in excess of any grant approved by and received from the MSBA shall be the sole responsibility of the Town. Any grant that the Town may receive from the MSBA for the Project shall not exceed the lesser (1) thirty six, and eighty-nine hundredths’ percent (36.89%) of eligible, approved Project costs, as determined by the MSBA, or (2) the total maximum grant amount determined by the MSBA, or act on anything relating thereto? (Inserted at the request of the 2025 School Building Committee) COMMENT: This Article seeks authorization to fund the replacement of the roof systems at South Elementary School (“South”). The existing roof systems are of varying ages and conditions and have required repairs and maintenance over time; much of the system has reached the end of its useful life. Recently, water infiltration from ice dams required an emergency response. The proposed Project is being developed in conjunction with the Massachusetts School Building Authority (“MSBA”) Accelerated Repair Program. Background South was constructed in 1948. The school roof is approximately 57,000 square feet. The building underwent an extensive expansion and renovation in 1998 at which point the school’s roofing systems were also completely replaced. Since that time the district has maintained it mainly through targeted repairs, with an emergency repair performed as recently as summer 2025. A 2022 study performed by Habeeb & Associates, the Town’s professional consultants, found that most of the 13 sections of the roofing (and the associated drainage fixtures) needed repair, and noted that the roof systems had exceeded their 20-year warranty. The report further noted that all roofing sections were approaching the end of their standard 25-year life expectancy and thus should be replaced in the near to intermediate term. As part of this roof Project Habeeb & Associates has been contracted to conduct a peer review of all design materials being submitted through the MSBA process. 2025 Annual Town Meeting authorized $320,000 for a schematic design study for the anticipated roofing systems replacement. The Town was subsequently accepted into the MSBA Accelerated Repair Program, and an Owner’s Project Manager was selected by the MSBA. All six public school buildings are actively required to accommodate current and projected student enrollment, based on Hingham Public Schools' facility evaluations and long-term planning. Overall enrollment is experiencing an increase, and over the next 10 years, elementary enrollments are projected by New England School Development Council (“NESDEC”) to increase by 304 students. 5 Building Study and Design Process To-Date Following the Town's acceptance into the MSBA's Accelerated Repair Program, the Project's design consultant, Gale Associates (“Gale”), was engaged to evaluate the roof and develop a schematic design. The April, 2026, evaluation included a visual assessment of the roofing and flashing; limited exploratory openings; hazardous-material sampling; an infrared drone survey; and a structural feasibility study. A related Massachusetts Architectural Access Board (“MAAB”) evaluation was subsequently conducted in early May, 2026. A whole roof system assessment study found that many portions of the South roof sub-structure are sound. Original timber framing installed in 1948, does not meet current snow-load Building Code (“Code”) requirements, and requires structural augmentation. In addition, several framing members in the 1998 expansion are very close to their maximum capacity (98%), and Gale recommended structural augmentation for that portion of the building as well. The remaining portions of the roof framing and decks are generally capable of supporting current code-required loads, although several framing members require reinforcement due to insufficient capacity for the additional load of future solar panels. Although the Town is not obligated to install solar panels, under the MSBA grant program, the roof structure must have a designated solar-ready area with sufficient capacity to support solar panels. The evaluation further found that most of the asphalt shingle and low-slope membrane roofing areas are more than 20 years old and showing signs of deterioration, including damaged shingles, poor-condition roof coatings, previous repairs related to water infiltration, and deteriorated flashing, sealants, and masonry. While the existing standing-seam metal roofing is generally serviceable, replacing it as part of the Project would provide a uniform, warrantable, and betterinsulated roof system. Limited hazardous-material testing found no asbestos in the samples collected, although additional testing will be required as the project progresses. Lead-based paint was identified on a roof truss, and the Project budget includes an allowance for potential abatement of both asbestos and lead. Lower-cost coating and overlay options for the existing roofing systems were also considered. These options were not recommended because they would not address the underlying deterioration and would require continued maintenance and repairs. The study concluded that continued patching and repairs would not provide a durable, long-term solution. The recommended approach is to replace the roof systems and address related flashing, masonry and drainage problems at the same time. Following Gale’s review, roof-covering options and cost comparisons were reviewed with Hingham Public Schools and the 2025 School Building Committee (“SBC”) in public meetings in June 2026. The SBC voted to proceed with PVC membrane roofing on the low-slope areas and standing-seam metal panels on the steep-slope areas. That direction, combined with findings on the age and condition of the existing systems, culminated in a Schematic Design submitted to the MSBA on August 27, 2026, and revised on September 18, 2026; this Schematic Design is the basis for the scope and cost estimate presented in this Article. Proposed Project The proposed Project will replace the existing roofing systems down to the roof decks, with the decks inspected and repaired as needed. The work will include new low-slope and steep-slope 6 roofing systems, along with related improvements to roof edges, flashing, drainage, gutters and downspouts, and rooftop equipment. The Project will also include reinforcement of selected roof framing and related interior work to meet current Code requirements and support potential future solar installation in the designated areas. Because the proposed roof assemblies will be thicker than the existing assemblies, related modifications will be required to drainage, roof-edge and flashing systems, as well as portions of the masonry. The work will also include masonry repairs, replacement of deteriorated sealants, and replacement or modification of existing roof ladders and other roof-access components. Because the Project cost exceeds 30% of the building’s assessed value, the Project must address accessibility throughout the building, not just in areas directly affected by the roof work. Thus, the Project will include accessibility improvements identified through a review of the school for compliance with applicable MAAB requirements. The preliminary scope includes modifications to toilet-room accessories, door hardware, portions of the exterior ramp and sidewalk, handrails, signage, vestibule flooring, doors and thresholds, and water coolers. Proposed Project Cost Based on the current Schematic Design, the total Project cost is $8,576,727, an increase from the $5,400,000 estimate presented at the 2025 Annual Town Meeting. The study and evaluation of the existing roof identified additional needs, most notably the augmentation of the wood-framed roof and structural steel trusses. The expanded scope was not contemplated in the previous estimate and has been incorporated into the current Project cost. Furthermore, Project costs have increased significantly over the past two years, reflecting continued construction cost escalation and broader inflationary pressures affecting labor and materials. Major cost elements include: Item / Category Estimated Cost Construction $7,064,575 Soft Costs (Feasibility, Admin, Design Fees, etc.) $1,123,600 Contingencies (Construction & Owner Project Manager) $ 388,552 Total Project Budget $8,576,727 The Project may not exceed the authorized amount without further authorization by Town Meeting. Final design development, MSBA review, and construction bidding will occur within this authorized Project budget. Financing This Project is being pursued through the MSBA Accelerated Repair Program, which is a nonentitlement, discretionary program. Reimbursement is based on eligible and approved Project costs. In accordance with MSBA requirements, this Article seeks authorization for the full Project cost of up to $8,576,727. The maximum MSBA grant is 36.89% of eligible, approved Project costs. Eligible, approved costs are presently estimated to be $7,787,441, resulting in an estimated 7 MSBA reimbursement of $2,872,787. The projected Town share would be approximately $5,703,940. This would be funded through excluded debt, which is exempt from the property tax cap under Proposition 2½. Excluded debt requires a 2/3 vote of Town Meeting and a majority ballot vote for adoption. If this Article is approved, the associated excluded debt service would result in an estimated FY28 property tax increase of approximately $55 for the average assessed-value home ($1,367,000) in addition to the annual property tax increase allowed under Proposition 2½. Hours Contact Search FY27 Budget Info/Schedule October 2026 Town Meeting Warrant - Text Home Committees Finance Committee October 2026 Town Meeting Warrant - Text October 2026 Town Meeting Warrant - Text In the name of the Commonwealth you are hereby required to notify and warn the inhabitants of the Town of Holliston who are qualified to vote in Town Affairs to meet in the Holliston High School Auditorium, 370 Hollis Street, Holliston, MA: MONDAY, OCTOBER 19, 2026 at 7:00 p.m. to act on the following Articles, to wit: ARTICLE 1: GENERAL STABILIZATION FUND SPONSORED BY: Select Board ESTIMATED COST: $150,000 To see if the Town will vote to raise and appropriate or transfer from available funds a sum of money for the General Stabilization Fund; or take any action relative thereto. SELECT BOARD COMMENTS: The balance of the General Stabilization Fund as of July 1, 2026 is $10.96 million. With no planned use within the Warrant below, the projected ending balance of the fund after October l Town Meeting would be $11.11 million, or 14.49% of the FY27 budgeted expenditures. This Article ensures that the balance of the General Stabilization Fund stays within range of the Town’s Financial Policies as updated in September 2024, specifically moving funds to stay above the target of 12% of General Fund Expenditures, but below the maximum ratio of 18%. ($150,000 from Free Cash) THE FINANCE COMMITTEE RECOMMENDS THAT THE TOWN APPROPRIATE $150,000 FROM FREE CASH TO THE GENERAL STABILIZATION FUND (UNANIMOUS) ARTICLE 2: PENSION STABILIZATION FUND SPONSORED BY: Select Board ESTIMATED COST: $250,000 To see if the Town will vote to raise and appropriate or transfer from available funds a sum of money for the Pension Stabilization Fund; or take any action relative thereto. SELECT BOARD COMMENTS: The May 2021 Annual Town Meeting established a fund to address the unfunded liability associated with pensions of municipal employees. State statute dictates that pension systems must be fully funded by 2040, and both the Middlesex County Retirement System (MCRS) and the Massachusetts Teachers Retirement System (MTRS) are approximately 60% funded. The Fund will allow the Town to address its unfunded liability while continuing to meet its current obligations. Should the legally required contributions to MCRS increase significantly in future years, this fund can also be used to protect the Town from negative budget impacts related to meeting this obligation. With an estimated fiscal year starting balance of $1.92 million, this appropriation would bring the balance to approximately $2.17 million, invested with the State’s PRIT system, consistent with the Town’s OPEB Trust Fund. ($250,000 from Free Cash) THE FINANCE COMMITTEE RECOMMENDS THAT THE TOWN APPROPRIATE $250,000 FROM FREE CASH TO THE PENSION STABILIZATION FUND (UNANIMOUS) ARTICLE 3: CAPITAL EXPENDITURE FUND SPONSORED BY: Select Board ESTIMATED COST: $2,100,000 To see if the Town will vote to raise and appropriate or transfer from available funds a sum of money for the Capital Expenditure Fund; or take any action relative thereto. SELECT BOARD COMMENTS: The Capital Expenditure Fund (CapEx) is used to fund capital expenses. An illustrative example of those capital expenses can be found under the Capital Budget (Article 11) in this Warrant. If all capital items utilizing CapEx funding in Articles 11 are approved, as presented in the warrant, the fund balance will be approximately $1.60 M million after October Town Meeting – assuming at least $2.1 million in Free Cash is available for appropriation by this article. This is the working estimate the Town has used for preparation for the Fall Town Meeting. The balance cannot be drawn down below $1.5 million or the Town would be at risk of conflicting with the Financial Policies (Min. Balance is 2% of Operating Expenditures). Article 11 below is the only proposed use of CapEx funding in October 2025. (Estimated $2,100,000 from Free Cash, pending final certification of Free Cash by the Department of Revenue) THE FINANCE COMMITTEE RECOMMENDS THAT THE TOWN APPROPRIATE $2,309,670 FROM FREE CASH AND $1,000,000 FROM ARTICLE 19 OF THE AY 2025 TOWN MEETING TO THE CAPITAL EXPENDITURE FUND (UNANIMOUS) ARTICLE 4: CLASSIFICATION PLAN: POSITION TITLE CHANGES SPONSORED BY: Select Board To see if the Town will vote to amend the job classification plan for full and part-time employees effective July 1, 2026 as approved at the May 2026 Annual Town Meeting by adding the following position title: POSITION PROPOSED GRADE Permitting Coordinator 400 ,or take any other action relative thereto. SELECT BOARD COMMENTS: The addition of this job title allows the town’s Planning Department to change the job title of the Administrative Clerk that supports the department to “Planning Coordinator.” The Administrative Clerk was also approved at a Grade 400 at the May 2026 Annual Town Meeting, so there is no financial impact or additional resources needed to make this change. This change would be part of a larger effort to better define the responsibilities of the role ARTICLE 5: PERSONNEL BYLAW AMENDMENT: DEFINITIONS SPONSORED BY: Select Board To see if the Town will vote to amend Section 3 of the Consolidated Personnel By-Law by inserting the following definition after Holiday Pay: Immediate Family: The immediate family shall consist of the employee’s father, mother, relative residing in the same household, father-in-law, mother-in-law, sister, brother, spouse, child, grandparents, and grandchildren. SELECT BOARD COMMENTS: This amendment adds a definition of immediate family to the Personnel Bylaw, which mirrors the definition included in collective bargaining agreements. ARTICLE 6: PERSONNEL BYLAW AMENDMENT: SORI REQUIREMENTS SPONSORED BY: Select Board To see if the Town will vote to amend Section 6 of the Consolidated Personnel By-Law to read as follows: SECTION 6: BACKGROUND CHECK For the mutual protection of the Town and its employees, successful candidates for employment, as the Town Administrator may require, shall be subject to a background check, which may include, but not be limited to, a criminal history background check (C.O.R.I.) and/or a sexual offender history check (S.O.R.I.). The Town Administrator shall review the background check to determine, in their discretion, whether it impacts the decision to employ the candidate. , or take any other action relative thereto. SELECT BOARD COMMENTS: This proposed amendment to the personnel by-law allows for the Town to run SORI checks for individuals seeking employment in positions with potential unmonitored contact with vulnerable populations. This practice modernization is aimed at protecting residents and the Town. ARTICLE 7: PERSONNEL BYLAW AMENDMENT: VACATION ACCRUALS SPONSORED BY: Select Board To see if the Town will vote to amend Sections 9, 10, and 11 of the Consolidated Personnel By-Law to read as follows: (deleted language shown in strikethrough and new language underlined): SECTION 9: VACATION POLICY Vacation leave may be taken when it is accrued, for a given fiscal year may be taken at any time during the fiscal year subject to the approval of the department head or other appropriate authority. Ten days two weeks of vacation leave may be carried over from one fiscal year to another, with the approval of the Town Administrator. Vacation leave with pay shall not be granted to temporary, on-call or seasonal employees. SECTION 10: VACATION LEAVE FOR FULL-TIME PERMANENT EMPLOYEES Vacation leave shall be granted to full-time permanent employees as follows: a. Effective July 1, 2027, vacation leave will accrue monthly, beginning on an employee’s date of hire, based on service completed during the previous month. of one (1) week with full pay shall be granted to any employee who has been employed by the town for at least six (6) full calendar months as of the first day of July following the employee’s date of hire. Employees with less than six (6) full calendar months of employment as of July 1 following their date of hire will be credited with a prorated amount of the one week of vacation time on that July 1. b. Vacation leave of two (2) weeks per year with full pay will accrue monthly for employees with 0 – 5 years of service. shall be granted to any employee who has been employed by the town for twelve (12) full calendar months as of July 1 of a given year. c. Vacation leave of three (3) weeks per year with full pay will accrue monthly for employees with 6 – 10 years of service. shall be granted to any employee who has been employed by the town for five (5) full years as of July 1 of a given year. d. Vacation leave of four (4) weeks per year with full pay will accrue monthly for employees with 11 – 15 years of service. shall be granted to any employee who has been employed by the town for twenty (20) full years as of July 1 of a given year. e. Vacation leave of five (5) weeks per year with full pay will accrue monthly for employees with 16 or more years of service. shall be granted to any employee who has been employed by the town for twenty (20) full years as of July 1 of a given year. f. Full pay, as used in this section, refers to the employee's regular straight-time salary or wages based on the rate paid at the time vacation pay is drawn. g. Vacation leave provided on July 1 of a given year is earned on a prorated monthly basis during the previous Fiscal Year. Employees who separate from Town employment will receive payment for any unused but accrued earned vacation leave. h. No more than 10 days (2 weeks) of vacation leave may be carried over from one year to the next. SECTION 11: VACATION LEAVE FOR PART-TIME EMPLOYEES Part-time permanent employees shall be entitled to prorated vacation leave based on the ratio of their part-time employment to full-time employment within their department. Vacation credited as of July 1 will be based upon the number of hours worked the previous fiscal year. , or take any other action relative thereto. SELECT BOARD COMMENTS: These proposed amendments seek to update current vacation policies that are out of date and not competitive. Under the “annual accrual” process currently in place, an employee hired in July would not receive their two weeks of vacation time until after the first year of employment. This has resulted in the Town losing highly qualified candidates in recent months. ARTICLE 8: PERSONNEL BYLAW AMENDMENT: PERSONAL TIME ACCRUALS SPONSORED BY: Select Board To see if the Town will vote to amend Section 12 of the Consolidated Personnel By-Law to read as follows: (deleted language in strikethrough and proposed new language underlined: SECTION 12: LEAVES OF ABSENCE Leaves of absence may be granted to permanent employees during a calendar year subject to the following provisions: a. Three two (2) days leave of absence with full pay shall be granted to permanent employees for personal business during any fiscal calendar year with written approval of the department head, and shall be requested at least twenty-four (24) hours prior to the date selected. Effective January 1, 2027, all permanent employees will be credited with 1.5 personal days, and then with 3 personal days on July 1, 2027, and on every July 1 thereafter. Personal time must be used by the end of the fiscal year it is earned and cannot be carried over. b. Except as otherwise provided in this By-Law, all other leaves of absence shall be without compensation and shall be subject to the written approval of the department head and Town Administrator, c. Permanent employees are allowed to take up to six (6) days leave with pay during any calendar year to attend to illness in the employee's immediate family. Such leave shall be deducted from the employee's sick leave. d. Statutory and certain other types of leaves of absence can be found in the Town’s Personnel Policies (See Town Website for Policies). , or take any other action relative thereto. SELECT BOARD COMMENTS: This proposed amendment has two objectives. First, it would grant personal days on a fiscal year basis, as opposed to on a calendar year basis. This would bring personal time in line with the way the Town grants vacation and sick time for eligible employees. The proposal also increases the personal days granted annually to eligible employees from two days to three days, which is comparable to nearby municipalities. ARTICLE 9: PERSONNEL BYLAW AMENDMENT: SICK & BEREAVEMENT LEAVE SPONSORED BY: Select Board To see if the Town will vote to amend Section 17 of the Consolidated Personnel By-Law to read as follows (deleted language in strikethrough and proposed new language underlined: SECTION 17 BEREAVEMENT LEAVE Bereavement leave with full pay, not to exceed five (5) days, in the discretion of the employee’s department head, may be granted to any permanent employee for a death in the employee’s immediate family. For purposes of this section, the immediate family shall consist of the employee’s father, mother, domestic partner, significant other residing in the same household, father-in-law, mother-in-law, sister, brother, spouse, child, grandparents and grandchildren. For the purposes of this section, the immediate family shall consist of the employee’s father, mother, relative residing in the same household, father-in-law, mother-in-law, sister, brother, spouse, child, grandparents, and grandchildren. This section shall also apply to parents who suffer loss of pregnancy. , or take any other action relative thereto. SELECT BOARD COMMENTS: This article would update Section 17 of the Personnel Bylaw with the language proposed in Article 6, while also adding language allowing for bereavement to be granted to parents suffering loss of pregnancy. ARTICLE 10: PERSONNEL BYLAW AMENDMENT: TOWN MANAGER ACT SPONSORED BY: Select Board To see if the Town will vote to amend the Consolidated Personnel By-Law to reflect the passage of the Town Manager Act both by the Massachusetts General Court and the Holliston October 2024 Town Meeting, by changing any references to “Town Administrator” to “Town Manager” and updating the position description for consistency therewith, or take any other action relative thereto. SELECT BOARD COMMENTS: This amendment simply updates the pertinent section and other references to the Town Administrator in the Personnel By-law to reflect the adoption of the Town Manager Act. ARTICLE 11: CAPITAL BUDGET SPONSORED BY: Select Board ESTIMATED COST: $3,172,030 To see if the Town will vote to raise and appropriate, transfer from available funds or borrow a sum of money for the purpose of capital expenditures, including replacement of old vehicles and equipment, for the following departments: Public Safety, Police, Fire, Public Works, Facilities, Information Technology, and Schools, including the expenditures listed below, and authorize the Select Board to trade or sell equipment toward part of the purchase price; or take any action relative thereto. Expenditure Police Vehicles (2 Cruisers, 1 Hybrid Admin.) - Capex - $207,100 Structural Firefighting Gear - Capex - $39,930 Fingerprinting System - Capex - $40,000 EV Replacement – Chevy Blazer - Capex - $52,000 Door Access Controls (Library) - Capex - $15,000 Door Access Controls (1750 Washington) - Capex - $37,000 Wastewater Treatment Plant SCADA - Capex - $24,000 Wireless Network Access Points - Capex - $50,000 Sander Body Replacement - $51,000 1 Ton Dump Truck - Capex - $121,000 Grounds Equipment Replacement Chromebooks - Capex - $30,000 Middle School Dishwasher - Capex - $50,000 Woodland Street Campus Exterior Door Replacements - Capex - $300,000 High School Supplies – Schedule Change - Capex - $50,000 Science Curriculum Updates - Capex - $30,000 Lead/Copper Service Line Replacements - Water Enterprise: Retained Earnings - $100,000 Water Main Replacements: Concord/High, Northway, Goulding/Adam Wheeler - Water Enterprise: Infrastructure Account - $1,800,000 Total: $3,172,030 SELECT BOARD COMMENTS: Using the Town's Capital Improvement Plan as a guiding document, it is the custom of the Town to fund and appropriate to departments specific project requests during the October Town Meeting. As referenced in the comments of Article 3, if Article 3 passes as written and all remaining of the items proposed to be funding out of the Capital Expenditure Fund are approved in Article 11, the remaining balance of the fund will be $1,602,433 – assuming an estimated deposit into the fund of $2,100,000 pending Free Cash certification. The $100,000 proposed appropriation from the Water Enterprise Retained Earnings is for the purposes of maintaining compliance with the EPAs' Lead Service Line Compliance Plan. The plan requires that all water services connected to the Holliston water system be physically verified to be absent of lead and/or galvanized steel. If present, service connections require replacement. This requires physical excavations of the service at the town curb stop. To date the Town has completed 50 excavations. There are 3038 public side services requiring excavation with a total 5018 total connected services. This is an on-going project with the next EPA milestone deadline of November 1, 2027 with the deliverable of a baseline inventory and the lead service line plan. Additional appropriations will be sought to complete the work and meet the EPA’s timeframe. The proposed $1,800,000 appropriation from the Water Enterprise Infrastructure Account is for the purposes engineering and construction related costs for water main replacements. Locations include Concord Street at High Street, Norland Street, the intersection of Goulding Street and Adam Wheeler Road and Adam Wheeler Road. These locations have been identified as high priority replacements due to the frequency of water main breaks, presence of non-operating and/or leaking gate valves and continued service disruptions. Work includes the design component and construction costs including but not limited to furnishing all necessary labor, materials, equipment and incidentals to install, test, disinfect and place in service approximately 2,500 linear feet of 8-inch ductile iron water mains, valves, hydrants, fittings, water services, culvert crossings, surface restoration and other related work ($1,272,030 from Capital Expenditure Fund, $100,000 from the Water Enterprise Retained Earnings Account, and $1,800,000 from the Water Enterprise Infrastructure Account) THE FINANCE COMMITTEE RECOMMENDS THAT THE TOWN APPROPRIATE $1,272,030 FROM THE CAPITAL EXPENDITURE FUND, $100,000 FROM THE WATER ENTERPRISE FUND, AND $1,800,000 FROM THE WATER ENTERPRISE INFRASTRUCTURE ACCOUNT FOR THE ITEMS LISTED IN THE ABOVE TABLE (UNANIMOUS) ARTICLE 12: COMMUNITY PRESERVATION FUND SPONSORED BY: COMMUNITY PRESERVATION COMMITTEE ESTIMATED COST: $209,000 To see if the Town will vote to transfer from available community preservation funds a sum of money for the following uses; or take any action relative thereto. Project Stoddard Park: Engineering Study for ADA Accessibility, Erosion Control, and Horizontal Infrastructure - $94,000 Central Fire Station: Window and Stucco Restoration -$115,000 Senior Center Sensory Garden - $125,0090 Total: $209,000 THE FINANCE COMMITTEE RECOMMENDS THAT THE TOWN APPROPRIATE $94,000 FROM THE COMMUNITY PRESERVATION GENERAL RESERVE FOR THE STODDARD PARK ENGINEERING STUDY, $115,000 FROM THE HISTORIC RESOURCES RESERVE FOR THE RESTORATION AND REPAIR OF THE STUCCO FAÇADE AND WINDOWS AT THE CENTRAL FIRE STATION, AND $125,000 FROM THE GENERAL RESERVE FOR THE EXPANSION AND RENOVATION OF OUTDOOR SPACE AT THE SENIOR CENTER (UNANIMOUS) ARTICLE 13: CENTRAL FIRE STATION SOLAR ARRAY PURCHASE SPONSORED BY: Select Board ESTIMATED COST: $421,500 To see if the Town will vote to transfer a sum of … CENTRAL FIRE STATION SOLAR ARRAY PURCHASE SPONSORED BY: Select Board ESTIMATED COST: $421,500 To see if the Town will vote to transfer a sum of money from Article 22 of the May 2024 Town Meeting to pay costs of acquisition, temporary … purchase agreement ("PPA") with a third party for the construction and installation of a solar panel array on the top of the Holliston Fire Department's headquarters at 59 Central Street. The roof is in dire need of repair, and Town … over $100,000 in charges triggered by the temporary relocation and disconnection of the solar panels while roof repairs were underway. Alternatively, the Town now has the option to purchase the asset from the third party for $111,283. text: Town of Milton 2026 Special Town Meeting Monday, October 19, 2026 Milton High School Auditorium 7:30 p.m. WARRANT INCLUDING THE REPORT OF THE WARRANT COMMITTEE AND RECOMMENDATIONS ON ARTICLES as required by Chapter 75, Section 1, of the General Bylaws of Town PLEASE BRING THIS REPORT TO TOWN MEETING October 2026 Special Town Meeting Warrant Commonwealth of Massachusetts, SS County of Norfolk To any of the constables of the Town of Milton in said County: GREETINGS: In the name of the Commonwealth of Massachusetts, you are hereby required to notify and warn the inhabitants of the Town of Milton, qualified to vote in Town affairs, to meet at the Milton High School Auditorium at 25 Gile Road in said Milton on Monday, the nineteenth day of October, 2026, next at 7:30 o’clock in the evening, then and there to act upon the following Articles to wit: Articles 1-9 And you are directed to warn said inhabitants qualified as aforesaid to meet at the times and places and for the purposes herein mentioned by posting attested copies of the Warrant in each of the Post Offices of said Town fourteen days before the nineteenth day of October and verify the Warrants are available to read and download on the Town’s website and paper copies are available at the Select Board’s Office, the Council on Aging, and the Milton Public Library at least fourteen days before the nineteenth day of October. Hereof fail not and make due return of this Warrant with your doings thereon to the Town Clerk, on or before the fifth day of October 2026. Given under our hands at Milton this of 22nd day of September, 2026. Winston A. Daley Meghan E. Haggerty Peter C. Obersheimer John E. Driscoll, Jr. Megan K. Nolan A True Copy: Attest William J. Neville Constable of Milton 3 INDEX WARRANT ARTICLES AND RECOMMENDATIONS ARTICLE NO 1 2 3 4 5 6 7 8 9 Title Amend Fiscal Year 2027 Appropriations Appropriation of Surplus Bond Proceeds Appropriation for Water System Improvements Community Preservation Committee Project Recommendation Zoning Bylaw Amendment: Chapter 275, Section 3.25 – MBTA Communities Multi-family Overlay District, P3 Acquisition of 303 Adams Street (Labouré College) School Building Committee Appropriation Amend Fiscal year 2027 PEG Access Enterprise Fund Appropriation Citizens’ Petition: Surveillance Technology 4 Page 10 11 12 13 14 15 18 19 20 In compliance with the American with Disabilities Act, this Warrant can be made available in alternative formats. The October 19, 2026, Special Town Meeting, if requested, will be offered by assisted listening devices or an interpreter certified in sign language. Requests for alternative formats should be made as far in advance as possible. Should you need assistance, please notify the SELECT BOARD at 617-898-4843 or 617-696-5199 TTY. Smoking and other tobacco use is prohibited in school facilities and outside on the school grounds by MGL Chapter 71, Section 37H, “An Act Establishing the Education Act of 1993.” This law applies to any individual at any time. Strong fragrances cause significant adverse reactions in some people, such as migraine headaches. Products with strong fragrances include personal care products such as perfume, cologne, fragranced hair products, after shave lotion, scented hand lotion, etc. Attendees at Town Meeting are requested to avoid wearing products with strong fragrances. As an accommodation to persons with such adverse reactions, and to allow safe and free access to the auditorium, the lobby and restroom, attendees at Town Meeting who are wearing products with strong fragrances, or who think they may be wearing products with strong fragrances, are requested to sit away from the sections nearest to the lobby entrance. 5 MESSAGE FROM THE TOWN MODERATOR Welcome to the 2026 October Special Town Meeting! Milton routinely holds Special Town Meetings for the purpose of addressing certain articles prior to the next Annual Town Meeting. During this October Special Town Meeting, there are nine (9) articles for your review and consideration. Articles 1-3, 6-8 were submitted by the Select Board. Article 4 was submitted by the Community Preservation Committee (CPC). Article 5 was submitted by the Planning Board. Article 9 was submitted by Citizens’ Petition. The Warrant Committee has reviewed each article and has provided its comments. If applicable, any Warrant Committee comments not included in this warrant will be available on the Town Meeting website prior to October 19, 2026, and hard copies will be provided on green sheets at Town Meeting. Please carefully review each article and direct any questions to the submitting party prior to Town Meeting. As is customary, I will co-host a show with our Warrant Committee Chair, Jay Fundling, on Milton Access Television and available on YouTube prior to Town Meeting. During this show, Mr. Fundling and I will discuss the articles in detail. The October Special Town Meeting will proceed subject to the rules that were approved at the Annual Town Meeting and printed in the Annual Town Meeting Warrant. Please review those rules carefully, as they will not be repeated during Town Meeting. In keeping with the rules set forth in the Annual Town Meeting Warrant, proposed amendments are to be submitted to the Moderator prior to Town Meeting. Specifically, such amendments should be submitted by the Moderator at or before 3:00 PM EST on Thursday, October 15, 2026, to afford adequate time for review by the Moderator, Town Counsel, the submitting party, and/or the Warrant Committee, as appropriate. Proposed amendments submitted after 3:00 PM EST on October 15 may or may not be permitted, at the discretion of the Moderator. In addition, as is customary, all presentations must be pre-approved, and presentations and requests to present are required to be submitted to the Moderator prior to Town Meeting. Accordingly, requests to present and copies of presentations must also be provided to the Moderator by no later than 3:00 PM EST on Thursday, October 15, 2026. Presentation requests and presentations submitted after 3:00 PM EST on October 15 may or may not be permitted, at the discretion of the Moderator. 6 You may contact the Moderator directly with any questions, concerns, or requests at edillon@miltonma.gov. Town Meeting will be governed by Volume 4 of Town Meeting Time. I look forward to seeing you in person at the October Special Town Meeting, beginning on Monday, October 19, 2026 at 7:30 PM EST at Milton High School. Sincerely, /s/ Elizabeth S. Dillon Elizabeth Dillon, Town Moderator 7 REPORT OF THE WARRANT COMMITTEE FOR THE 2026 OCTOBER SPECIAL TOWN MEETING Greetings to the Honorable Select Board, Town Meeting members and Residents of the Town of Milton: The Warrant Committee herein presents to the Town Meeting recommendations for action on Articles submitted to the Special Town Meeting convening on Monday, October 19, 2026. There are nine articles for this Special Town Meeting. These Articles address a variety of issues that concern the Town beyond the typical zoning matters we historically address at Town Meeting. There are five articles submitted by the Select Board, one article submitted by the Planning Board, one article submitted by the Community Preservation Committee, and one article submitted by a Citizens’ Petition. The Warrant Committee has reviewed all articles and suggests the Town take action on the first eight articles, while sending the ninth back to the Select Board for study. For each article, the Warrant Committee’s recommendation in bold is the motion before Town Meeting and the place where Town Meeting will begin its discussion. Article 1 allocates additional state funds that were not expected when we approved the 2026-27 budget at the last Annual Town Meeting. This article allocates this money to the Reserve Fund. Article 2 reallocates funds borrowed for certain projects - but ultimately not needed for those projects to other projects. Article 3 authorizes the town to spend to improve water mains in coordination with other adjacent projects. These projects may be funded with 0% MWRA loans. Article 4 authorizes the CPC to fund a playground improvement at Tucker School. Article 5 clarifies the MBTA zoning to state that there be a minimum of 15% Affordable Housing in the larger developments. Articles 6 and 7 are both related to the possible purchase of the former Labouré College property located at 303 Adams Street. Article 6 is the approval of the purchase itself. This article requests Town Meeting’s approval to purchase the property at the price of $11,750,000 negotiated by the Select Board. Such purchase will then require the approval of a debt exclusion measure by the registered voters of the Town at a later date. 8 A potential plan for the town’s use of this property is to alleviate the schools’ overcrowding at a potentially more affordable cost than the current proposed project on Gile Road. Article 7 provides funding to the School Building Committee for a study to thoroughly examine the option of a school on this location and compare the two alternatives. Article 8 amends the appropriation from the PEG Access Enterprise Fund for Fiscal Year 2027. The Warrant committee supports all the above Articles, as described further in the comments below. Article 9 is a petition submitted by over 100 citizens regarding the use of surveillance technology in town. The Warrant Committee discussed this petition with the Police Chief, who noted that the way that the article is worded could have unintended negative consequences. It is our understanding that the Select Board will be examining this issue in the near future, probably before this Special Town Meeting. We recommend this issue be taken up for study by the Select Board and not voted on at this meeting. Throughout the Warrant you will see the Warrant Committee’s recommendations printed in bold. While these recommendations are an important part of the Warrant Committee’s job, they are not the most important part. More important than telling you what the Warrant Committee recommends is telling you why we recommend it. You – the legislative body of the Town, representing all Town voters – will make the ultimate decision on all of these articles. The Warrant Committee endeavors to provide you, through our written comments and our presentations before Town Meeting, the reasons why we made the decisions we did, along with enough information to make your decision on our recommendation. You may agree with some of our recommendations, and you may disagree with others. But if we have provided you with enough information to efficiently and confidently make your decision, then the Warrant Committee will consider its job done. The Chair wishes to express his appreciation to the members of the Warrant Committee for the many hours of work required to prepare this Warrant. The Warrant Committee also extends thanks to the Town Administrator, Mr. Nicholas Milano, the Select Board, the Planning Board, and all the other departments throughout the Town for their continued assistance in our mandate. The Chair is especially grateful for the assistance of the Warrant Committee Clerk, Karen Bosworth. LeeMichael McLean Nicole Boyson Rukstalis Lindsey Sands Ronald Sia Jimmy Stournaras Nicholas Tangney Cecille Yang Jay Fundling, Chair Elaine Craghead, Secretary Jamesley Dasse Lorraine Dee Lawrence Johnson Liveda Johnson Andrew Koh Macy Lee Karen Bosworth, Clerk 9 ARTICLE 1 To see by what sum of money the Town will vote to amend the appropriations voted at the 2026 Annual Town Meeting for the twelve-month period beginning July 1, 2026; and to determine how said appropriations shall be raised, whether by transfer from available funds or otherwise; and to act on anything related thereto. Submitted by the Select Board. RECOMMENDED that the Town vote to amend the following appropriation voted by the 2026 Annual Town Meeting by the article referenced in the table below, and in the manner identified below, for the twelve-month period beginning July 1, 2026: Department Reserve Fund 2026 ATM Article 27 Current FY2027 Appropriation $300,000 FY2027 Adjustment $363,469 Revised FY2027 Appropriation $663,469 And that to meet said appropriation the sum of $363,469 be raised from the tax levy. COMMENT: In developing the budget for the fiscal year, the Town relies upon the state aid forecast in the Governor’s budget which is released in mid to late January; however, the final state budget is not typically approved until late June each year. In some years, the final state aid figures vary from the Governor’s original proposal. For Fiscal Year 2027, the final net state aid to Milton (after subtracting for state assessments) is projected to be $14,175,116, an increase of $363,469 (or 2.6%) from the Governor’s proposed budget. This article would amend the Fiscal Year 2027 Budget by appropriating this additional revenue to the Fiscal Year 2027 Reserve Fund, which is set aside for extraordinary or unanticipated expenses. Transfers from the Reserve Fund are subject to the approval of the Warrant Committee and may be transferred to any budget account. In Fiscal Year 2026, the Reserve Fund was used to help offset that year’s snow and ice removal deficit as well as two smaller unanticipated expenses. The final Fiscal Year 2027 net state aid amount of $14,175,116 is a $692,950, or a 5.1%, increase over Fiscal Year 2026. 10 ARTICLE 2 To see if the Town will vote to authorize the following transfers of surplus bond proceeds: (1) Transfer $350,001.35 of surplus proceeds from previously issued bonds which are no longer needed to complete the DPW Locker Room and Cemetery Garage project for which they were initially borrowed, to pay the costs of purchasing a replacement Fire Engine, as authorized by M.G.L. c. 44, §20; (2) Transfer $74,000.00 of surplus proceeds from previously issued bonds which are no longer needed to complete the Pine Tree Brook flood control dam rehabilitation project for which they were initially borrowed, to pay the costs of purchasing a replacement Fire Engine, as authorized by M.G.L. c. 44, §20; Submitted by the Select Board. RECOMMENDED that the Town vote to approve the article as printed in the Warrant. COMMENT: If the Town issues debt for projects, but does not fully use all of the borrowed funds for a project (referred to as “surplus bond proceeds”), there are several options by which the Town can apply those funds to expenses. For surplus bond proceeds less than $50,000, the Select Board may vote to apply them to debt service expenses. For surplus bond proceeds greater than $50,000, a Town Meeting vote is required to appropriate the surplus proceeds to another capital project. This article proposes to appropriate surplus proceeds from projects for which the funds are no longer needed to offset the cost of the acquisition of a replacement Fire Engine (to replace Engine 2 which operates out of the East Milton Station). An appropriation of $1.1 million for the replacement of Engine 2 was approved at the 2025 Annual Town Meeting with an expected delivery in Winter 2026. This article would result in the Town using $424,001.35 in surplus proceeds towards Engine 2’s replacement costs, reducing the maximum amount the Town would borrow from $1.1 million to $675,998.65. 11 ARTICLE 3 To see what sum of money the Town will vote to appropriate for the rehabilitation, replacement or enhancement of the Town's water system, and to authorize the Select Board, on behalf of the Town, to apply for and use federal, state, MWRA or other funds for this purpose, to determine how such appropriation shall be raised; whether by borrowing or otherwise; and to act on anything relating thereto. Submitted by the Select Board. RECOMMENDED that the sum of $2,280,000 be appropriated for the purpose of financing the rehabilitation, replacement or enhancement of the Town's water system, including costs incidental and related thereto; that to meet this appropriation, the Treasurer, with the approval of the Select Board, is authorized to borrow $2,280,000 under and pursuant to Chapter 44, Section 8 (5) of the General Laws, as amended, or any other enabling authority, and to issue bonds or notes of the Town therefor, and that the Select Board and hereby is authorized to accept and expend in addition to the foregoing appropriation one or more grants or gifts from the Massachusetts Water Resources Authority or any other public or private funding source. COMMENT: As a member of the Massachusetts Water Resources Authority ("MWRA"), the Town has access to water system improvement funding through ten-year, 0% interest loans. This provides the primary source of funding for capital investments into the Town's watermains and requires appropriation by Town Meeting. The Town has previously appropriated $1,790,100 for water main improvements by votes of the Town Meeting at the 2024, 2025, and 2026 Annual Town Meetings. The Department of Public Works is preparing a package of water main improvement projects and is seeking the opportunity to increase the total appropriation available to complete more work as part of a larger bid package. The additional appropriation in this article would support replacement of aging water mains on Governors Road, Franklin Street, and Bassett Street. The Governors Road mains, originally installed in 1915 and 1932, experienced a water main break in May 2026 and have reached the end of their useful service life. The Franklin Street water main, installed in 1929, has experienced several breaks in recent years, highlighting the need for replacement. Replacing the water mains on Franklin and Bassett Streets at this time would allow the Town to coordinate utility and roadway improvements with the ongoing Franklin/Bassett apartment development. Completing this work concurrently will help reduce construction costs, improve project efficiency, and minimize future disruptions to residents, businesses, and the traveling public. Construction is anticipated to occur during the 2027 and 2028 construction season. Additional funding will enable the Town to address critical infrastructure needs proactively, improve system reliability, and reduce the likelihood of future emergency repairs and service disruptions. 12 ARTICLE 4 To see if the Town will approve a project and grant funding, as recommended by the Community Preservation Committee for Fiscal Year 2027, for the rehabilitation, restoration, and/or improvements to the playground at the Tucker School, provided that the project must enter into a Grant Agreement with the Town and submit regular progress and budget reports; and to act on anything relating thereto. text: TOWN OF PLYMOUTH FALL ANNUAL TOWN MEETING WARRANT Saturday, October 17, 2026 To the Town Clerk of the Town of Plymouth, Commonwealth of Massachusetts: GREETINGS: In the name of the Commonwealth, you are directed to notify and warn the Inhabitants of Plymouth, qualified to consider and vote on articles at the Fall Annual Town Meeting of the Town of Plymouth, to meet in a hybrid format, on Saturday, the Seventeenth day of October, 2026, at 8:00 a.m., with information necessary for the Moderator, Town Meeting members, Town officials and interested members of the public to access and witness the deliberations and actions taken at the Town Meeting as follows: Town Meeting members will have the option to be in person at Plymouth North High School at 41 Obery Street in Plymouth, MA using an electronic voting clicker to take actions or remotely using telecast through Zoom Webinar videoconferencing platform for their deliberations and the use of V-Voter to take actions remotely. Town Officials will provide information through the Zoom Webinar videoconferencing platform. Interested members of the public will be able to view the meeting through the Plymouth local government channel (The Local Seen) available on Comcast and Verizon, or thelocalseen.media/live. Individuals not otherwise lawfully entitled to speak will have the opportunity to speak through the Zoom Webinar videoconferencing platform with forty-eight (48) hours advanced notice given to and permission granted by the Town Moderator. Registered Town of Plymouth voters wishing to participate in the hybrid Fall Annual Town Meeting shall submit a request to participate in the Meeting to the Town Clerk not less than fortyeight (48) hours in advance of the Town Meeting scheduled for Saturday, October 17, 2026, commencing at 8:00 a.m. Upon receipt of the request and verification of the requester’s voter registration status, the Town Clerk shall provide to the requester instructions for participating in the remote Town Meeting. To act on the following articles to wit: ARTICLE 1: Budget Amendment – Visitor’s Center Capital Funds To see if the Town will vote to amend the vote taken under Article 4 Item A9 of the 2025 Fall Annual Town Meeting warrant to reduce the Capital appropriations for the Visitor’s Center Addition by a sum of money, or take any other action relative thereto. TOWN MANAGER ARTICLE 2: Budget Amendment – Solid Waste Enterprise To see if the Town will vote to amend the votes taken under Article 10 of the 2026 Spring Annual Town Meeting warrant, and, as necessary, to raise and appropriate, transfer from available funds, or borrow funds for the purpose of supplementing enterprise departmental expenses, and/or to reduce certain departmental expenses or otherwise amend said vote, or take any other action relative thereto. SELECT BOARD ARTICLE 3: Borrowing Authority Rescission Request To see if the Town will vote to rescind the remaining borrowing authority on Article 4B1 of the 2022 Spring Special Town Meeting, further amended by Article 10 of the 2023 Spring Special Town Meeting, for the Municipal Airport Sewerage Treatment Plant Upgrade, or take any other action relative thereto. SELECT BOARD ARTICLE 4: FY26 Snow and Ice Deficit Funding Recommendation To see if the Town will vote to raise and appropriate or transfer from available funds a sum of money to fund the Fiscal Year 2026 Snow & Ice deficit that remains from the June 30, 2026, balance sheet, or take any other action relative thereto. SELECT BOARD ARTICLE 5: Capital Recommendations To see if the Town will vote to raise and appropriate, transfer from available funds or borrow a sum of money for the construction and/or repair and/or purchase and/or lease and/or replacement of departmental buildings and/or equipment and/or capital facilities for various departments of the Town and/or for feasibility and other types of studies, including the payment of costs incidental or related thereto, and to authorize contracts or lease/purchase agreements for such purposes for terms of three or more years, as follows, ITEM A1 DEPARTMENT Finance PROJECT DESCRIPTION Communication Towers & Compound Maintenance Work A2 Purchase of a Motor Grader A6 Public Works – Highway Division Public Works – Maintenance Division Public Works – Maintenance Division Public Works – Maintenance Division Energy & Environment A7 Energy & Environment 0 Spooner Street Phase II Assessment A8 Energy & Environment Engineering & Permitting for Restoration of Gilmore Bogs A3 A4 A5 Parking Garage Repairs Town Hall Lighting Upgrade Main Library Transformer Replacement Downtown Resiliency Project A9 Public Works – Water Planning, Design and Permitting New Source Division or take any other action relative thereto. SELECT BOARD ARTICLE 6: Environmental Affairs Funding – Cyanobacteria Monitoring and Sampling To see if the Town will vote to raise and appropriate or transfer from available funds a sum of money to be used for ongoing monitoring and sampling of cyanobacteria blooms in local lakes and ponds, or take any other action relative thereto. DEPARTMENT OF ENERGY AND ENVIRONMENT ARTICLE 7: Environmental Affairs Funding – Town Forest Fire Department Overtime To see if the Town will vote to raise and appropriate or transfer from available funds a sum of money to be used for staffing two Fire Department brush breakers during the prescribed burn at Town Forest, or take any other action relative thereto. DEPARTMENT OF ENERGY AND ENVIRONMENT ARTICLE 8: Title Research Funding for Roads of Shallow Pond Estates To see if the Town will vote to raise and appropriate, transfer from available funds or borrow a sum of money for the purposes of title research, appraisals, legal fees, land surveying, drafting costs, and/or any other action required to prepare the roadways of Andrew’s Way, Barbara’s Way, Donna Drive, Kathleen Drive, Penny Lane, and Shallow Pond Way, for future acceptance as Public Ways, or take any other action relative thereto. DEPARTMENT OF PUBLIC WORKS ARTICLE 9: Change 2027 Spring Town Meeting Date To see if the Town will vote to reschedule the 2027 Spring Annual Town Meeting from April 3, 2027, to April 24, 2027, as required by General Bylaws, Ch. 50, §3, or to take any other action relative thereto. SELECT BOARD ARTICLE 10: Adoption of G.L. Ch. 39, §23D, Mullin Rule To see if the Town will vote to accept the provisions of G.L. Ch. 39, §23D, which provides that a member of a board, committee, or commission holding an adjudicatory hearing shall not be disqualified from voting in the matter solely due to the member's absence from one session of such hearing, provided that certain conditions are met; and provided further that such acceptance shall be applicable to all adjudicatory hearings opened on or after the effective date of the vote taken hereunder, or to take any other action relative thereto. TOWN MANAGER ARTICLE 11: Charter Amendment – Addition of Two Alternate Members to the Conservation Commission To see if the Town will vote to authorize the Select Board to petition the General Court to amend Section 3-10-1 of the current Charter in order to add two alternate members to the composition of the Conservation Commission by inserting the underlined as written below, provided, however, that the General Court may make clerical or editorial changes of form only to the bill, unless the Select Board approves amendments to the bill before enactment by the General Court, provided further that the Select Board is hereby authorized to approve amendments which shall be within the scope of the general public objectives, or, take any other action relative thereto. CHAPTER 3: THE EXECUTIVE BRANCH: THE SELECT BOARD, THE TOWN MANAGER AND PLANNING BOARD: Section 10: Conservation Commission 3-10-1: The Select Board shall appoint a Conservation Commission of seven (7) members and two (2) alternate members for three-year (3) overlapping terms. A B Revolving Fund Plymouth County Outreach (PCO) C D E Department, Board, Committee, Agency or Program or Activity Officer Authorized to Fees, Charges or Other Expenses Payable from Spend from Fund Receipts Credited to Fund Fund Fiscal Years Chief of Police POLICE DEPARTMENT Annual dues collected from PCO member departments PCO Initiative to assist Fiscal year 2020 those struggling with subsequent years substance abuse disorders, mental health disorders, and/or behavioral health disorders and ARTICLE 13: General Bylaws Amendment – Demolition Delay To see if the Town will vote to amend the General Bylaws, Ch. 180, Historic District and Historic Preservation, §5, Intent and Purpose, and §6, Definitions, by inserting the underlined and deleting the strikethrough as written below, or take any other action relative thereto. § 180-5. Intent and purpose. The Demolition Delay Bylaw is enacted for the purpose of preserving and protecting significant buildings and other structures (barns or out-buildings which are generally associated with the significantly historic building) within the Town of Plymouth which constitute or reflect distinctive features of the architectural, cultural, economic, political or social history of the Town and to limit the detrimental effect of demolition on the character of the Town. Through this bylaw, owners of preferably preserved buildings are encouraged to seek out alternative options that will preserve, rehabilitate or restore such buildings and residents of the Town are alerted to impending demolitions of significant buildings. By preserving and protecting significant buildings, streetscapes and neighborhoods, this bylaw promotes the public welfare by making the Town a more attractive and desirable place in which to live and work. To achieve these purposes, the Plymouth Historic District Commission Historical Commission is authorized to advise the Building Commissioner with respect to demolition permit applications. The issuance of demolition permits is regulated as provided by this bylaw. § 180-6. Definitions. As used in this article, the following terms shall have the meanings indicated: COMMISSION — The Plymouth Historic District Commission Historical Commission. Thereafter, each member shall serve a term of three (3) years. 2. The Community Events Committee may award grants for the purpose of encouraging and supporting events, projects, activities, and services that are of mutual interest to the residents of and visitors to Wareham. All such events, projects, activities, and services shall be nonexclusive and open to the public. The purpose of the Committee is to strengthen the Town by fostering community involvement and community spirit. 3. The Committee is authorized to expend, for the purposes set forth herein, all monies made available to it through the Community Events Fund, gifts, grants, or transfers of funds authorized by law, subject to all applicable procurement laws of the Commonwealth, the Wareham Home Rule Charter, and the Town of Wareham By-Laws., or to take any other action relative thereto. ARTICLE 9 AUTHORITY: Multi Member Board SPONSOR: Planning Board To see if the Town will vote to amend the Zoning Bylaw as follows, or act or do anything in relation thereto. 1) Amend Section VIL Accessory Apartments, by deleting the entire section and replacing it with Section VLL. Accessory Dwelling Unit (ADU), in the form set below: L. Accessory Dwelling Unit (ADU) The intent of this section of the bylaw is to 1) increase the diversity of housing options; 2) ‘encourage better utilization of existing housing stock; 3) curb the construction of illegal unregulated apartment units, and; 4) create an additional source of housing. An accessory dwelling unit (ADU) is a self-contained dwelling unit inclusive of sleeping, cooking and sanitary facilities constructed on the same lot as the principal dwelling, that maintains a separate entrance in accordance with the requirements of the Building Code for safe egress. Protected Use ADU — An ADU allowed by right and in accordance with the provisions of Section 8 of Chapter 150 of the Acts of 2024 and 760 CMR 71.00. A Protected Use ADU shall be no more than half the gross floor area of the principal dwelling or 900 s.f., whichever is smaller. A Protected Use ADU shall be permitted through the Building Department. Large Accessory Dwelling Unit (LADU) — An ADU that does not qualify as a Protected Use ADU, with a maximum gross floor area of 1,200 s.f. A LADU shall be permitted through the Special Permit process, and in accordance with the following bylaw provisions. a. Anattached or interior LADU shall be designed to maintain the appearance of the type of dwelling of which itis a part. . b. A detached LADU shall be clearly subordinate to the principal dwelling. This may be accomplished through size, placement, or design, or a combination of these elements. Only one (1) Protected Use ADU or LADU'shall be allowed per lot. Protected Use ADUs and LADUs may be utilized as short-term rentals if the land owner resides on the property. 2) Amend Section 1B — Definitions, to add definitions of Gross Floor Area (GFA) and Short-term Rental in the form set forth below: ‘ Gross Floor Area (GEA): The sum of the areas of all stories of the building of compliant ceiling height pursuant to the Building Code, including basements (finished or unfinished), lofts, and intermediate floored tiers, measured from the interior faces of exterior walls or from the centerline of walls separating buildings or dwelling units but excluding crawl spaces, garage parking areas, attics, enclosed porches and similar spaces. Short-term Rental: A furnished residential unit that is rented out for a period of 31 consecutive days or less, not including tenancies at will, or month to month leases. 3) Amend Section IML.A. Planning Board voted 5-0-0 to recommend that Town Meeting approve this article. Commentary: . Residents have been confused with Mass law Protected Use ADUs versus local accessory apartments. Amendments standardize terms and make regulation of both more uniform.
